docs.title: ENUMs Usage Reference — RustMT4
docs.text: Every enumeration the RustMT4 API uses, with exact values and where it appears. All are generated into metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api by prost.

docs.title: How enums work here
docs.text:
prost generates each proto enum as a Rust #[repr(i32)] enum. Request fields that are enums are plain i32, so you cast when building a request:

use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let req = pb::OpenedOrdersRequest {
    sort_type: pb::EnumOpenedOrderSortType::SortByOpenTimeAsc as i32,   // enum → i32
};

Reply fields that are enums are also i32; compare with Variant as i32, or decode with the generated try_from.

MT4Service casts these for you — e.g. opened_orders(sort) takes the typed EnumOpenedOrderSortType directly.

docs.title: 1. EnumAccountTradeMode — account type
docs.text:
Used by: account_summary → AccountSummaryData.account_trade_mode.

Variant Value Meaning AccountTradeModeDemo 0 Demo account AccountTradeModeContest 1 Contest account AccountTradeModeReal 2 Live account 
let a = account.account_summary().await?;
if a.account_trade_mode == pb::EnumAccountTradeMode::AccountTradeModeReal as i32 {
    println!("LIVE account — be careful");
}

docs.title: 2. EnumAccountMarginMode — margin calculation mode
docs.text:
Used by: account_summary → AccountSummaryData.account_margin_mode.

Variant Value Meaning AccountMarginModeRetailNetting 0 Netting (parity with MT5) AccountMarginModeExchange 1 Exchange AccountMarginModeRetailHedging 2 Hedging

MT4 is always hedging (several positions per symbol). The other values exist only for parity with MT5.

docs.title: 3. EnumOpenedOrderSortType — open-order sort
docs.text:
Used by: opened_orders → OpenedOrdersRequest.sort_type.

Variant Value SortByOpenTimeAsc 0 SortByOpenTimeDesc 1 SortByOrderTicketIdAsc 2 SortByOrderTicketIdDesc 3

docs.title: 4. EnumOrderHistorySortType — history sort
docs.text:
Used by: orders_history → OrdersHistoryRequest.input_sort_mode.

Variant Value HistorySortByOpenTimeAsc 0 HistorySortByOpenTimeDesc 1 HistorySortByCloseTimeAsc 2 HistorySortByCloseTimeDesc 3 HistorySortByOrderTicketIdAsc 4 HistorySortByOrderTicketIdDesc 5

docs.title: 5. EnumQuoteHistoryTimeframe — bar timeframe
docs.text:
Used by: quote_history → QuoteHistoryRequest.timeframe.

Variant Value Period QhPeriodM1 0 1 minute QhPeriodM5 1 5 minutes QhPeriodM15 2 15 minutes QhPeriodM30 3 30 minutes QhPeriodH1 4 1 hour QhPeriodH4 5 4 hours QhPeriodD1 6 1 day QhPeriodW1 7 1 week QhPeriodMn1 8 1 month

⚠️ Ordinal 0–8, not MQL minute counts. H1 is 4, not 60.

docs.title: 6. OrderSendOperationType — order direction/type (requests)
docs.text:
Used by: order_send → OrderSendRequest.operation_type.

Variant Value Meaning OcOpBuy 0 Market buy OcOpSell 1 Market sell OcOpBuylimit 2 Buy limit OcOpSelllimit 3 Sell limit OcOpBuystop 4 Buy stop OcOpSellstop 5 Sell stop

Same numbering as MQL4 OP_BUY..OP_SELLSTOP.

docs.title: 7. OrderCloseDeleteMode — what a close/delete did (reply)
docs.text:
Used by: order_close_delete → OrderCloseDeleteData.mode.

Variant Value Meaning OcdMarketOrder 0 A market order was closed OcdPendingOrder 1 A pending order was deleted

docs.title: 8. ServerTimezoneSource — where the UTC offset came from (reply)
docs.text:
Used by: server_timezone → ServerTimezoneData.source.

Variant Value Meaning Unknown 0 Not read yet; utc_offset_seconds stays unset Live 1 Read by this terminal LastValidated 2 Last validated offset for this broker, used until this terminal reads its own

docs.title: 9. Mt4SubEnumEventGroupType — streaming event group (reply)
docs.text:
Used by: on_trade → OnTradeData.type; on_opened_orders_profit → OnOpenedOrdersProfitData.type (access as d.r#type).

Variant Value OrderProfit 0 OrderUpdate 1

docs.title: 10. SubOrderOperationType — order type in stream frames (reply)
docs.text:
Used by: on_trade / on_opened_orders_profit order rows → .type (OnTradeOrderInfo, OnOpenedOrdersProfitOrderInfo).

Variant Value Meaning SubOpBuy 0 Buy SubOpSell 1 Sell SubOpBuylimit 2 Buy limit SubOpSelllimit 3 Sell limit SubOpBuystop 4 Buy stop SubOpSellstop 5 Sell stop

docs.title: Not an enum, but you'll decode it: order_type
docs.text:
OpenedOrderInfo.order_type and HistoryOrderInfo.order_type are plain i32, not a named proto enum — but they follow the same 0 Buy, 1 Sell, 2 BuyLimit, 3 SellLimit, 4 BuyStop, 5 SellStop numbering. MT4Sugar decodes them via OrderType::from_i32, which also exposes .is_market() / .is_buy().

use metarpc_mt4::OrderType;
let positions = orders.iter().filter(|o| matches!(OrderType::from_i32(o.order_type), Some(t) if t.is_market()));

See also: MT4Account — Master Overview · Return Codes · MT4Service API

docs.title: Getting Started with RustMT4
docs.text: Quick setup & overview — start automating MetaTrader 4 with RustMT4 (Rust + gRPC) in minutes.

docs.title: 🎯 What is RustMT4?
docs.text: RustMT4 is a type-safe Rust client for MetaTrader 4 terminals over gRPC. No C++ DLL wrappers — direct, async, reliable programmatic trading.

docs.title: Three-layer architecture
docs.text:
Layer Type What you get MT4Account low Raw gRPC — build …Request, get …Data. Full control. MT4Service mid Friendly args (&str symbols, typed enums), clean returns. MT4Sugar high One-liners: buy/sell by side, pip math, risk sizing, trailing, watchers.

Each layer wraps the one below, so you can drop down a level any time you need more control.

docs.title: 📦 Installation
docs.text:
Not published on crates.io yet — clone the repo:

git clone https://github.com/MetaRPC/RustMT4.git
cd RustMT4

Build (requires the WinLibs GNU toolchain on Windows):

cargo build

docs.title: 🔑 API key & authentication
docs.text:
Connecting to the MetaRPC endpoint (mt4.mrpc.pro:443) needs an API key:

  1. Sign up (free): https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Generate a key in your dashboard: https://mrpc.pro/my → API Keys.
  3. Provide it via the MRPC_API_KEY environment variable (or api_key in settings.json). The SDK sends it on every call.

The terminal session id is handled for you: Connect returns a GUID, and the SDK attaches it to all later requests and streams automatically — no GetId call needed.

docs.title: 🔌 Minimal connection example
docs.text:
Compose the three layers (here, the top one) and read your balance:

use metarpc_mt4::{MT4Account, MT4Service, MT4Sugar};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // host + port only; MRPC_API_KEY is read from the environment.
    let sugar = MT4Sugar::new(MT4Service::new(MT4Account::new("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443)));

    // login, password, broker server name, optional terminal label, connect timeout (s)
    sugar.connect_by_server_name(12_345_678, "password", "FreshForex-Demo", None, 120).await?;

    let a = sugar.get_account_info().await?;
    println!("Balance: {:.2} {}  Equity: {:.2}", a.balance, a.currency, a.equity);

    sugar.disconnect(false).await?;
    Ok(())
}

Prefer the raw layer? MT4Account::new("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443) then account.account_summary().await? (returns AccountSummaryData with account_balance, account_equity, …).

docs.title: RustMT4 Glossary
docs.text: The terms you'll meet across these docs — architecture, MT4 trading, Rust/async, and gRPC — each with a one-paragraph definition and where it shows up in the SDK.

docs.title: Three-layer architecture
docs.text:
RustMT4 is split into three stacked layers, each wrapping the one below:

Layer Type Role MT4Account low Raw gRPC — build …Request, get …Data. MT4Service mid Friendly args, clean returns. MT4Sugar high One-liners, pip math, risk sizing.

docs.title: MT4Account
docs.text: Layer 1. Owns the gRPC channel, TLS, request metadata (session id + API key), retry and reconnect. Methods take raw protobuf requests and return raw …Data. Use it for full control.

docs.title: MT4Service
docs.text: Layer 2. The same 25 operations with friendly arguments (&str symbols, typed sort enums) and clean returns (a Vec or scalar instead of a wrapper struct). Streams are renamed stream_*.

docs.title: MT4Sugar
docs.text: Layer 3. ~45 convenience methods: buy/sell by side, pip conversions, risk-based lot sizing, trailing/breakeven, watchers, order info. Reuses the plain DTOs in src/models.rs.

docs.title: Orchestrator / Preset
docs.text: An orchestrator (run_* in src/strategies/) chains Sugar calls into a full lifecycle (size → enter → manage → close). A preset configures it: StrategyPreset (what to trade) + RiskPreset (how much to risk). See Strategies.

docs.title: Order vs Position
docs.text: In MT4 there's no separate "position" object: an open market order is the position. All open orders — market and pending — live in one list, told apart by order_type. MT4Sugar::positions() filters to the market ones; orders() returns everything.

docs.title: Order type
docs.text: An integer 0 Buy, 1 Sell, 2 BuyLimit, 3 SellLimit, 4 BuyStop, 5 SellStop (MQL4 OP_* numbering). Decoded by OrderType::from_i32 with .is_market() / .is_buy().

docs.title: Pending order
docs.text: An order that triggers when price reaches a level, rather than filling now: limit (buy below / sell above the market) and stop (buy above / sell below). Placed with buy_limit/sell_limit/buy_stop/sell_stop; deleted with close/cancel_pendings.

docs.title: Lot / Volume
docs.text: Trade size. 1.0 lot = trade_contract_size units (100,000 for FX majors). Brokers constrain it with volume_min, volume_max, volume_step — always pass sizes through normalize_lot.

docs.title: Point vs Pip
docs.text: A point is the smallest price step (SYMBOL_POINT, e.g. 0.00001 on a 5-digit pair). A pip is the conventional unit: point × 10 on 3/5-digit symbols, else point. MT4Sugar::pip_size computes it; pips_to_price / price_to_pips convert.

docs.title: Digits
docs.text: Price decimal places (5 for EURUSD, 3 for USDJPY). Round prices to this with normalize_price to avoid "invalid price" (129).

docs.title: Stop Loss (SL) / Take Profit (TP)
docs.text: Protective exit prices attached to an order — SL caps loss, TP locks profit. Set them as absolute prices (modify_sl_tp_by_price) or as pip distances from entry (modify_sl_tp_by_pips). Must respect trade_stops_level or the broker rejects with 130.

docs.title: Spread
docs.text: ask − bid. In pips via MT4Sugar::spread_pips. Wide spreads (news, low liquidity) are a common reason to skip an entry.

docs.title: Swap
docs.text: Interest credited/debited for holding a position overnight (swap_long / swap_short per lot). Part of an order's net result: profit + swap + commision.

docs.title: Margin / Equity / Free margin / Margin level
docs.text: Margin is collateral reserved by open positions; equity = balance + floating P/L; free margin = equity − margin; margin level = equity / margin × 100. All on AccountSummaryData (account_summary). Unlike MT5, MT4's summary carries these directly.

docs.title: Magic number
docs.text: An integer tag you stamp on orders (set_defaults(magic, …)) to identify which bot/strategy owns them. Filter with orders_by_magic.

docs.title: Hedging
docs.text: Holding opposite positions on the same symbol at once. MT4 is always hedging (account_margin_mode = RetailHedging). Net two opposite orders with close_by to save a spread.

docs.title: Trailing stop / Breakeven
docs.text: Trailing ratchets the SL behind price as it moves in your favor (trail_stop, only ever tightening). Breakeven moves the SL to entry (±a few pips) once in profit (auto_breakeven, never loosening). Both are one-shot — call on a timer.

docs.title: Future / async / .await
docs.text: Every SDK method is async and returns a Future — a value that completes later. Nothing runs until you .await it inside a Tokio runtime. See The Async Model.

docs.title: Tokio
docs.text: The async runtime RustMT4 runs on. Start it with #[tokio::main]; sleep with tokio::time::sleep (never std::thread::sleep, which blocks the runtime).

docs.title: Result<T, MT4Error>
docs.text: Every call returns a Result. Ok(T) on success, Err(MT4Error) on failure — see Return Codes. Propagate with ?.

docs.title: tonic::Streaming<…Reply>
docs.text: A server stream — a long-lived subscription that pushes frames. Read with stream.message().await in a loop, matching the reply's oneof { Data, Error }. MT4Account returns these directly; MT4Sugar forwards them to channels.

docs.title: mpsc::Receiver
docs.text: A Tokio multi-producer/single-consumer channel. Sugar's watchers (subscribe_quotes, watch_profit, watch_tickets) spawn a task that forwards stream frames onto one; you rx.recv().await. Drop the receiver to unsubscribe.

docs.title: DTO (Quote, Bar, OrderResult, …)
docs.text: Plain Rust structs in src/models.rs that MT4Sugar returns instead of raw protobuf — friendlier fields, Serialize/Deserialize derived.

docs.title: gRPC
docs.text: The high-performance RPC framework the SDK speaks over HTTP/2 + TLS to mt4.mrpc.pro:443. Supports both unary (request/response) and server-streaming calls.

docs.title: Protobuf (protocol buffers)
docs.text: The binary message format for requests/replies. The generated Rust types live in metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api (via prost). MT4Account works with these directly.

docs.title: …Request / …Reply / …Data
docs.text: The call shape: you send a …Request, the server answers a …Reply whose response is a oneof { Data, Error }. MT4Account unwraps the Data payload (…Data) or turns Error into MT4Error.

docs.title: Session id (terminal GUID)
docs.text: A per-terminal identifier returned by Connect/ConnectEx. The SDK captures it and attaches it (with your API key) to every later request and stream — you never call GetId.

docs.title: API key (MRPC_API_KEY)
docs.text: Your MetaRPC authentication token, sent on every call. Provide it via the MRPC_API_KEY env var or api_key in settings.json. Get one at mrpc.pro/my.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: The config loader (src/config.rs): reads settings.json and overlays env vars (MT4_LOGIN, MT4_PASSWORD, MT4_SERVER, MT4_SYMBOL, MT4_NAME, MRPC_API_KEY — env wins). Fields: user, password, server_name, name, api_key, test_symbol.

docs.title: 🧰 SDK conveniences
docs.text:
Term What it is Auto-normalization normalize_lot / normalize_price round to the symbol's step/digits so the broker accepts the order. Risk-based sizing calc_lot_by_risk(symbol, cash, sl_pips) → the normalized lot that risks cash over the stop. Pip helpers pip_size, pips_to_price, price_to_pips, spread_pips. Watchers / Waiters Watchers stream values onto a channel; waiters poll until a condition holds (8. Watchers & Waiters). ensure_symbol Select a symbol and wait for a usable two-sided quote before trading it.

See also: Getting Started · Project Map · ENUMs Reference · Return Codes

docs.title: gRPC Streaming & Subscription Management
docs.text: How to subscribe to live data in RustMT4, consume it cleanly, and shut it down — the Rust/Tokio way.

docs.title: The model in one line
docs.text:
A streaming call returns a tonic::Streaming<…Reply>. You read frames with stream.message().await in a loop. To unsubscribe, drop the stream — there's no cancellation token or finally cleanup to remember. When the value goes out of scope, the subscription ends.

let mut stream = account.on_symbol_tick(pb::OnSymbolTickRequest {
    symbol_names: vec!["EURUSD".into()],
}).await?;

while let Ok(Some(reply)) = stream.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_symbol_tick_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response {
        if let Some(t) = d.symbol_tick { println!("{} {}/{}", t.symbol, t.bid, t.ask); }
    }
}
// stream dropped here → unsubscribed

docs.title: The five streams
docs.text:
On MT4Account (raw Streaming<…Reply>):

Method Pushes on_symbol_tick(req) live ticks for the given symbols on_trade(req) order/trade events (new / updated / removed) on_opened_orders_tickets(req) the open-order ticket list on a timer on_opened_orders_profit(req) per-order profit + account snapshot on a timer on_connect_state(req) terminal connection-state events

On MT4Service the same streams are renamed stream_ticks, stream_trades, stream_opened_tickets, stream_opened_profit, stream_connect_state (friendly args, same Streaming<…Reply>).

On MT4Sugar three of them are wrapped into mpsc channels of friendly values — see below.

docs.title: A) Raw loop (full control)
docs.text:
Match the reply's oneof { Data, Error } yourself:

use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let mut stream = account.on_symbol_tick(pb::OnSymbolTickRequest { symbol_names: vec!["EURUSD".into()] }).await?;
while let Ok(Some(reply)) = stream.message().await {
    match reply.response {
        Some(pb::on_symbol_tick_reply::Response::Data(d)) => { /* handle d */ }
        Some(pb::on_symbol_tick_reply::Response::Error(e)) => { eprintln!("stream error: {e:?}"); break; }
        None => break,
    }
}

docs.title: B) Sugar channel (simplest)
docs.text:
MT4Sugar spawns the loop for you and forwards values onto a tokio::mpsc channel. The background task ends on the first stream error or when you drop the receiver:

let mut rx = sugar.subscribe_quotes(vec!["EURUSD".into(), "GBPUSD".into()]).await?;
while let Some(q) = rx.recv().await {
    println!("{} {}/{}", q.symbol, q.bid, q.ask);
}

Also: sugar.watch_profit(1000) → OnOpenedOrdersProfitData, sugar.watch_tickets(1000) → OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData.

docs.title: Bounded consumption
docs.text: Streams run until you stop them. Common ways to bound them:

docs.title: Stop after N frames
docs.text:
let mut stream = account.on_symbol_tick(req).await?;
let mut n = 0;
while let Ok(Some(reply)) = stream.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_symbol_tick_reply::Response::Data(_)) = reply.response {
        n += 1;
        if n >= 10 { break; }   // drop(stream) on scope exit = unsubscribe
    }
}

docs.title: Stop after a timeout
docs.text:
Wrap the whole loop in tokio::time::timeout:

use std::time::Duration;

let _ = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), async {
    while let Ok(Some(reply)) = stream.message().await {
        // handle frames
    }
}).await;   // elapsed → future dropped → stream dropped → unsubscribed

docs.title: Stop on a condition
docs.text:
while let Ok(Some(reply)) = stream.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_symbol_tick_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response {
        if let Some(t) = d.symbol_tick {
            if t.bid >= 1.0950 { println!("target hit"); break; }
        }
    }
}

For "wait until price X" or "wait until filled", MT4Sugar already has wait_price / wait_filled / wait_closed.

docs.title: Filtering by enum
docs.text:
Stream frames carry the same enums as the rest of the API (see ENUMs Reference). Example — react only to closes on on_trade:

use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_trade(pb::OnTradeRequest {}).await?;
while let Ok(Some(reply)) = s.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_trade_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response {
        if let Some(ev) = d.event_data {
            for o in &ev.removed_orders {           // order closed/deleted
                println!("CLOSE #{} {} P/L {:+.2}", o.ticket, o.symbol, o.order_profit);
            }
        }
    }
}

OnTradeData.type / OnOpenedOrdersProfitData.type are the raw identifier r#type in Rust (Mt4SubEnumEventGroupType); order rows carry SubOrderOperationType (0 Buy … 5 SellStop).

docs.title: Multiple concurrent streams
docs.text:
Each stream is independent. Run several at once by spawning a task per stream, and coordinate shutdown with a channel or tokio::select!:

use std::time::Duration;

// ticks in the background
let mut rx = sugar.subscribe_quotes(vec!["EURUSD".into()]).await?;
let ticks = tokio::spawn(async move {
    while let Some(q) = rx.recv().await { println!("tick {} {}", q.symbol, q.bid); }
});

// profit in the foreground, with a deadline
let mut prof = sugar.watch_profit(1000).await?;
let _ = tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(30), async {
    while let Some(d) = prof.recv().await {
        if let Some(a) = d.account_info { println!("equity {:.2}", a.equity); }
    }
}).await;

ticks.abort();   // stop the background task (drops its receiver → unsubscribes)

tokio::select! lets one task react to whichever stream fires first:

tokio::select! {
    Some(q) = rx.recv()   => println!("tick {}", q.bid),
    Some(d) = prof.recv() => println!("profit frame"),
}

docs.title: Reconnection
docs.text:
Pair streams with on_connect_state to know when the broker link drops, and re-subscribe after a reconnect:

let mut cs = account.on_connect_state(pb::OnConnectStateRequest { terminal_ids: vec![] }).await?;
while let Ok(Some(reply)) = cs.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_connect_state_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response {
        if !d.is_connected { /* pause trading; re-open data streams after reconnect */ }
    }
}

The unary call wrapper already auto-retries transient transport errors and terminal-not-found; streams, being long-lived, are re-opened by your own logic.

docs.title: ✅ Do / ❌ Don't
docs.text:
✅ Do - Drop the stream (or receiver) to unsubscribe — it's deterministic. - Bound streams (break on N / condition, or tokio::time::timeout). - Handle the Error arm of the oneof. - Prefer one stream with many symbols over many single-symbol streams. - Use Sugar watchers (subscribe_quotes / watch_*) for the common cases.

❌ Don't - Don't std::thread::sleep inside an async task — use tokio::time::sleep. - Don't poll quote in a tight loop when a tick stream exists. - Don't assume "no frames" means "broken" — a quiet market simply sends nothing.

See also: MT4Account 5. Streaming Methods · MT4Sugar 8. Watchers & Waiters · The Async Model

docs.title: MT4 for Beginners: Your First Steps
docs.text: Welcome! This guide is for complete beginners who have never used MetaTrader 4. We'll set up the terminal and a free demo account, then point RustMT4 at it.

docs.title: What is MetaTrader 4 (MT4)?
docs.text:
MetaTrader 4 is a widely-used trading platform. It lets you:

  • Trade forex, metals, commodities and more
  • Analyze markets with charts and indicators
  • Run automated strategies
  • Monitor positions in real time

Think of MT4 as the "cockpit" for the markets. RustMT4 lets you control that cockpit programmatically from Rust, over gRPC.

docs.title: Why start with a demo account?
docs.text:
A demo account is a risk-free practice account with virtual money. We strongly recommend it while you learn:

  • ✅ Zero risk — virtual funds (typically $10,000–$100,000)
  • ✅ Real market conditions — live prices and behavior
  • ✅ Learn the platform before risking real money
  • ✅ Test your code — perfect for developing RustMT4 bots

docs.title: Live account
docs.text: A live account uses real money. Only move to live when you understand MT4, have tested your strategy thoroughly on demo, and accept the risks.

docs.title: Quick start: creating a demo account
docs.text: The fastest path is to create a demo account directly in the MT4 terminal.

docs.title: Step 1️⃣ — Download and install the MT4 terminal
docs.text:
1. Visit the official MetaQuotes site: https://www.metatrader4.com/en/download
  2. Download the build for your OS.
  3. Install and launch it.

docs.title: Step 2️⃣ — Launch MT4 and find the Navigator panel
docs.text:
On first launch MT4 usually shows a popup to open a new account. If it doesn't, find the Navigator panel.

The Navigator is on the left, below Market Watch. It has sections: Accounts, Indicators, Expert Advisors, and others.

docs.title: Step 3️⃣ — Open a new demo account
docs.text:
1. In Navigator, find Accounts.
  2. Right-click "Accounts".
  3. Choose "Open an account".

This opens the broker server search.

docs.title: Step 4️⃣ — Select the MetaQuotes demo server
docs.text:
In the broker search, for your first account use the simplest option:

  • Look for "MetaQuotes-Demo" / "MetaQuotes Ltd" (use the search field if needed).
  • Select it and click Next.

docs.title: Step 5️⃣ — Choose "Open a new demo account"
docs.text: Select "Open a new demo account" and click Next.

docs.title: Step 6️⃣ — Fill in your details
docs.text:
• Name / Last Name / Email
  • Phone — optional for demo
  • Deposit — virtual amount (e.g. $10,000)
  • Leverage — 1:100 is a good start
  • Currency — USD, EUR, …

Accept the terms and click Next.

docs.title: Step 7️⃣ — Save your credentials
docs.text:
MT4 creates the account and shows:

  • Login — account number (e.g. 591129415)
  • Password — master (trading) password
  • Investor Password — read-only

docs.title: Return Codes & Errors Reference — RustMT4
docs.text:
How failures reach you in RustMT4, and the MQL4 trade-error codes behind rejected orders.

⚠️ MT4 uses MQL4 error codes (0–150 for the trade server, 4000+ for MQL runtime) — not the MT5 ENUM_TRADE_RETCODE numbers (10004, 10018, 10019, …). If you've seen those, they belong to MT5.

docs.title: How errors surface
docs.text:
RustMT4 doesn't return a status code you have to inspect — a failed call returns Err(MT4Error). Everything is one error enum (src/error.rs):

pub enum MT4Error {
    ConnectionError(String),
    AuthError(u64),
    TradeError(u32, String),     // MQL trade failure: code + message
    Io(std::io::Error),
    Grpc(tonic::Status),         // transport / HTTP2
    Transport(String),
    Api { code: String, message: String, mql_code: i32, mql_desc: String, error_type: i32 },
    InvalidLogin(String),        // never retried
    Protocol(String),
    NotConnected,
}
  • Grpc — transport level. Unavailable / DeadlineExceeded / Cancelled are retried automatically.
  • Api — the gateway answered with its Error oneof (a gateway code string plus an MQL code/description). TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND triggers one reconnect + retry.
  • InvalidLogin — wrong login/password. Never retried — repeated bad logins get accounts locked.
  • TradeError — an order_send / order_modify / order_close_delete was rejected on the MQL side. MT4Sugar::place_order maps a non-zero mql_code into this variant.

No error ≠ nothing to check only for reads. For trades, a returned Ok means it executed; a rejection comes back as Err(TradeError|Api), so handle the Result.

docs.title: The gateway Error payload
docs.text:
When a call fails server-side, the reply's Error oneof carries (proto Error):

Field Rust Meaning error_code String Gateway code, e.g. TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND, CONNECT_EX_INVALID_LOGIN_ERROR error_message String Human-readable message mql_error_int_code i32 The MQL4 error number (see tables below) mql_error_description String MQL4 error text type i32 ErrorType category

MT4Error::from_api turns this into InvalidLogin (for login/password failures) or Api { .. } otherwise.

docs.title: MQL4 trade-server error codes
docs.text:
These are the ones you'll actually hit from trading calls (mql_code). Source: the generated MqlErrorCode enum.

Code Name Meaning / fix 0 ERR_NO_ERROR Success 1 ERR_NO_RESULT No error, but nothing changed (e.g. modify to identical values) 2 ERR_COMMON_ERROR Generic error — retry / check connection 3 ERR_INVALID_TRADE_PARAMETERS Bad request fields 4 ERR_SERVER_BUSY Trade server busy — back off and retry 6 ERR_NO_CONNECTION No link to the trade server 8 ERR_TOO_FREQUENT_REQUESTS Throttle your calls 128 ERR_TRADE_TIMEOUT Trade timed out — may still have executed; reconcile 129 ERR_INVALID_PRICE Price off/stale — normalize price, re-quote 130 ERR_INVALID_STOPS SL/TP too close — respect trade_stops_level 131 ERR_INVALID_TRADE_VOLUME Lot invalid — normalize to volume_step/min/max 132 ERR_MARKET_CLOSED Market closed — wait for session 133 ERR_TRADE_DISABLED Trading disabled for the account/symbol 134 ERR_NOT_ENOUGH_MONEY Insufficient margin — smaller lot 135 ERR_PRICE_CHANGED Price moved — re-quote and resend 136 ERR_OFF_QUOTES No prices — symbol not live / illiquid 137 ERR_BROKER_BUSY Broker busy — retry 138 ERR_REQUOTE Requote — resend at the new price, or raise slippage 139 ERR_ORDER_LOCKED Order already being processed 140 ERR_LONG_POSITIONS_ONLY_ALLOWED Only buys allowed on this symbol 141 ERR_TOO_MANY_REQUESTS Too many requests — throttle 145 ERR_TRADE_MODIFY_DENIED Modify denied (too close to market / frozen) 146 ERR_TRADE_CONTEXT_BUSY Trade context busy — serialize trade calls 147 ERR_TRADE_EXPIRATION_DENIED Expiration not allowed by broker 148 ERR_TRADE_TOO_MANY_ORDERS Order count limit reached 149 ERR_TRADE_HEDGE_PROHIBITED Hedging not allowed 150 ERR_TRADE_PROHIBITED_BY_FIFO FIFO rule violated

Codes 4000+ (ERR_NO_MQLERROR, ERR_ARRAY_INDEX_OUT_OF_RANGE, …) are MQL runtime errors from the terminal side — rare for API trading. The full set is in the MqlErrorCode enum.

docs.title: Inspect the code
docs.text:
MT4Error has helpers so you don't parse strings:

use metarpc_mt4::MT4Error;

match sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", 0.10, None, None).await {
    Ok(r)  => println!("opened #{}", r.ticket),
    Err(e) => {
        if e.is_market_closed() {                 // mql_code == 132
            println!("market closed — try later");
        } else if e.mql_code() == 134 {
            println!("not enough money — size down");
        } else if e.is_retryable() {              // transient transport / terminal-not-found
            println!("transient — safe to retry: {e}");
        } else {
            eprintln!("failed: {e}");
        }
    }
}
Helper True when mql_code() returns the MQL4 number (Api.mql_code or TradeError code), else 0 is_market_closed() MQL 132 or a "market closed" message is_retryable() transient transport or terminal-not-found is_terminal_not_found() gateway lost the terminal (reconnect + retry) api_code() the gateway code string (empty for non-API errors)

docs.title: What's retried for you
docs.text:
The client's call wrapper auto-retries: transient gRPC (Unavailable/DeadlineExceeded/Cancelled) and TERMINAL_INSTANCE_NOT_FOUND (one reconnect). Trade calls are not retried blindly — a timed-out order_send may have filled, so on error you reconcile with opened_orders / positions before resending.

See also: ENUMs Reference · order_send · MT4Sugar 5. Order Entry

docs.title: The Async Model — How RustMT4 Executes
docs.text: RustMT4 is async all the way down: every call returns a future you .await. This page explains the model and when each pattern fits.

docs.title: 🎯 Everything is async
docs.text:
The SDK runs on the Tokio runtime. There is no synchronous API — every method on MT4Account, MT4Service and MT4Sugar is async and must be .awaited inside a Tokio context:

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let sugar = MT4Sugar::new(MT4Service::new(MT4Account::new("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443)));
    sugar.connect_by_server_name(12_345_678, "password", "FreshForex-Demo", None, 120).await?;
    let a = sugar.get_account_info().await?;          // await a request/response call
    println!("Balance: {:.2} {}", a.balance, a.currency);
    Ok(())
}

docs.title: Two shapes of async call
docs.text: Shape What it is How you consume it Request / response account_summary(), quote(), order_send() let x = call(...).await?; Server stream on_symbol_tick(), stream_opened_profit() loop on stream.message().await, or a Sugar watcher's mpsc::Receiver

docs.title: Request / response
docs.text:
One round trip, one value back. Sequential by default:

let q = sugar.last_quote("EURUSD").await?;
let lots = sugar.calc_lot_by_risk("EURUSD", 50.0, 20.0).await?;

docs.title: Streaming
docs.text:
A long-lived subscription that pushes frames. Read it in a loop, or let MT4Sugar forward it to a channel:

let mut rx = sugar.subscribe_quotes(vec!["EURUSD".into()]).await?;
while let Some(q) = rx.recv().await {
    println!("{} {}/{}", q.symbol, q.bid, q.ask);
}

See gRPC Streaming for the full patterns.

docs.title: 🚀 Running work concurrently
docs.text:
Because calls are non-blocking, independent work overlaps. Quote several symbols at once with tokio::join!, or spawn a management task while the main flow continues:

// concurrent, not sequential
let (a, b) = tokio::join!(
    sugar.last_quote("EURUSD"),
    sugar.last_quote("GBPUSD"),
);
let (eur, gbp) = (a?, b?);

// background trailing loop
let handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
    loop {
        let _ = sugar.trail_stop(ticket, 15.0).await;
        tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_secs(2)).await;
    }
});

For many symbols, prefer a batched call (quote_many, one stream_ticks with all names) over many single calls.

docs.title: 💡 Rules of thumb
docs.text:
• Always .await — a future that isn't awaited does nothing.
  • One stream, many symbols beats many single-symbol streams.
  • Don't block the runtime — avoid std::thread::sleep; use tokio::time::sleep.
  • Waiters poll every 500 ms (wait_price, wait_filled) — convenience, not low latency. For hot paths, subscribe to ticks.

See also: gRPC Streaming · MT4Sugar 8. Watchers & Waiters

docs.title: Step 0 — API key
docs.text:
Connecting to mt4.mrpc.pro:443 needs a key:

  1. Register (free): https://mrpc.pro/signup.
  2. Generate a token: https://mrpc.pro/my.
  3. Export it: set MRPC_API_KEY=... (Windows) / export MRPC_API_KEY=... (bash).

cd RustMT4

docs.title: Step 2 — The code
docs.text:
The three-layer client. MT4Sugar gives you the shortest path to a trade:

use metarpc_mt4::{MT4Account, MT4Service, MT4Sugar};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    // host + port; MRPC_API_KEY comes from the environment.
    let sugar = MT4Sugar::new(MT4Service::new(MT4Account::new("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443)))
        .set_defaults(1001, 20, "my-first-bot");   // magic, slippage (points), comment

    // login, password, broker server name, optional label, timeout (s)
    sugar.connect_by_server_name(12_345_678, "password", "FreshForex-Demo", None, 120).await?;
    println!("Connected to MT4!");

    let a = sugar.get_account_info().await?;
    println!("Balance: {:.2} {}", a.balance, a.currency);

    // make sure the symbol is live, then buy 0.01 lot at market
    sugar.ensure_symbol("EURUSD", std::time::Duration::from_secs(10)).await?;
    let r = sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", 0.01, None, None).await?;
    println!("Order sent! Ticket #{} @ {}", r.ticket, r.price);

    // 20-pip stop, 40-pip target (direction-aware, by pips from entry)
    sugar.modify_sl_tp_by_pips(r.ticket, Some(20.0), Some(40.0)).await?;

    sugar.disconnect(false).await?;
    Ok(())
}

Demo accounts only while you learn — buy_market sends a real order on whatever account you connect.

docs.title: MT4Account — Master Overview
docs.text:
One page to orient fast: the low-level async gRPC client for MetaTrader 4. Jump to any group overview or method spec from here.

MT4Account is Layer 1 — direct gRPC/protobuf calls to the MT4 terminal gateway. MT4Service (typed facade) and MT4Sugar (high-level helpers) build on top of it.

It exposes 25 feature methods across 5 groups (plus connection helpers). Defined in src/mt4/account.rs.

MT4, not MT5. MT4 is order-based: there are no separate "positions" — a filled market order is the position, and pending orders live in the same list. Symbol properties come in one bulk symbol_params_many call rather than per-property getters.

docs.title: 🚦 Start here — Section Overviews
docs.text:
• 1. Account Information — balance/equity snapshot, trade statistics, equity curve, unrealized-P/L extrema.
  • 2. Orders & History — open orders (market + pending), their tickets, and closed-order history.
  • 3. Symbols & Quotes — symbol list, Market Watch select, bulk params, ticks, bar history, server timezone.
  • 4. Trading Operations — send, modify, close/delete, and close-by.
  • 5. Streaming Methods — real-time server streams: ticks, trade events, ticket lists, per-order profit, connection state.

docs.title: 🔌 Usage pattern (Rust, async)
docs.text:
MT4Account is async (tokio): each call builds the protobuf request, attaches the id + apikey metadata, and returns the reply's typed …Data, or an MT4Error.

use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;
use metarpc_mt4::MT4Account;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let account = MT4Account::new("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443); // api key from MRPC_API_KEY / "TRIAL"
    account.connect_by_server_name(12_345_678, "password", "FreshForex-Demo", None, 120).await?;

    let s = account.account_summary().await?;
    println!("{:.2} {} eq {:.2}", s.account_balance, s.account_currency, s.account_equity);

    let q = account.quote(pb::QuoteRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
    println!("bid/ask {:.5}/{:.5}", q.bid, q.ask);

    account.disconnect(false).await?;
    Ok(())
}

docs.title: 🧱 How the call contract works
docs.text:
Every feature method:

  1. builds the protobuf …Request (many MT4 requests have optional fields — pass ..Default::default()),
  2. attaches the id + apikey metadata,
  3. calls the right tonic service client,
  4. unwraps the reply — each …Reply carries a oneof { Data, Error }, returned as Result<…Data, MT4Error>.

So you always get the typed …Data directly. Friendly argument shapes live in MT4Service and MT4Sugar.

docs.title: 🔐 Constructor & connection
docs.text:
MT4Account::new(host: impl Into<String>, port: u16) -> MT4Account

Connect by broker server name (cluster, e.g. "FreshForex-Demo"):

account.connect_by_server_name(login, "password", "FreshForex-Demo", Some("my-label"), 120).await?;

Pass a stable terminal label (Some("…")) so re-runs reuse the same terminal. reconnect() re-establishes the session with the stored parameters; disconnect(delete) stops it (delete = true removes it permanently).

docs.title: 🧩 Layer map
docs.text:
Layer Type What it adds 1 — low-level MT4Account raw gRPC, auto-metadata, typed …Data returns 2 — facade MT4Service friendly args (&str, sort enums), clean values 3 — high-level MT4Sugar order construction, pip math, risk sizing, management

See also: Getting Started · Return Codes · ENUMs Reference

docs.title: 1. Account Information — Overview
docs.text:
The account's money picture and trading statistics: a one-call snapshot, aggregated stats, the equity curve, and per-order unrealized-P/L extrema.

These methods are read-only. account_summary lives on mt4_term_api.AccountHelper; the rest on mt4_term_api.TradeStats. Each returns a typed …Data payload.

docs.title: Methods in this group
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner account_summary() AccountSummaryData Balance, equity, margin, leverage, currency, trade mode — one round-trip. trade_stats(req) StatsData Aggregated trade statistics (drawdown, profit factor, Sharpe, …). trade_stats_equity_history(req) StatsWithChartsData Stats plus equity points and per-trade series. equity_history(req) EquityHistoryData Just the equity-curve points. trade_unrealized_pl(req) TradeUnrealizedPlData Max/min unrealized P/L reached per open order.

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text:
• Startup banner / pre-trade snapshot → account_summary().
  • Performance report (win rate, drawdown, profit factor) → trade_stats().
  • Draw an equity curve → equity_history() (or trade_stats_equity_history() for stats + curve in one call).
  • How far each open trade swung → trade_unrealized_pl().

Unlike MT5, this AccountSummaryData does carry margin / free-margin / margin-level directly.

The stats requests all accept an optional from (server time, yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss) or from_utc — send one, not both; omit for the full account history.

Back to: MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Account Summary (RECOMMENDED)
docs.text:
Complete account snapshot — balance, equity, margin, leverage, currency, trade mode — in a single call.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::account_summary() (defined in src/mt4/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: AccountSummary(AccountSummaryRequest) -> AccountSummaryReply
  • Payload: AccountSummaryData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. One call that returns every essential account property.
  • Why you need it. The most efficient way to read balance/equity/margin at once — one round-trip.
  • When to use. At session start (banner / sanity check), and before any risk decision or order.

As a side effect it caches the server→UTC shift (account.server_utc_shift_secs()), used to convert gateway timestamps.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn account_summary(&self) -> Result<pb::AccountSummaryData, MT4Error>

No arguments. Returns the typed payload, or an MT4Error.

Request / Reply:

message AccountSummaryRequest {}
message AccountSummaryReply { oneof response { AccountSummaryData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — AccountSummaryData (key fields)
docs.text: Field Rust type Description account_login i64 Account number account_balance f64 Balance (excludes floating P/L) account_equity f64 Equity = balance + floating P/L account_credit f64 Credit account_margin f64 Margin used account_margin_free f64 Free margin account_margin_level f64 Margin level, percent account_leverage i64 Leverage (e.g. 100 = 1:100) account_currency String Deposit currency account_user_name String Account owner account_company_name String Broker account_trade_mode i32 0 demo / 1 contest / 2 real account_trade_allowed bool Trading allowed for the account account_trade_expert bool EA trading allowed is_investor bool Connected with the investor (read-only) password server_time Option<Timestamp> Broker server time utc_server_time_shift_minutes i32 Server offset from UTC, minutes

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One call beats many. Balance, equity, margin and leverage come together.
  • balance vs equity. equity − balance is your current floating P/L.
  • Margin is here. Unlike MT5, you don't need a separate call for margin / free-margin / level.
  • Snapshot, not a stream. Re-query before a risk check.

docs.title: 1) Session-start banner
docs.text:
let s = account.account_summary().await?;
println!("#{}  {}  balance {:.2} {}  equity {:.2}  (floating {:+.2})",
    s.account_login, s.account_company_name, s.account_balance, s.account_currency,
    s.account_equity, s.account_equity - s.account_balance);
println!("leverage 1:{}  free margin {:.2}  level {:.1}%", s.account_leverage, s.account_margin_free, s.account_margin_level);

docs.title: 2) Trade-mode guard
docs.text:
let s = account.account_summary().await?;
if s.account_trade_mode == 2 { println!("REAL account — be careful"); }
if !s.account_trade_allowed { println!("trading is disabled on this account"); }

docs.title: 3) Margin-level alert
docs.text:
let s = account.account_summary().await?;
if s.account_margin > 0.0 && s.account_margin_level < 200.0 {
    println!("[ALERT] margin level {:.0}%", s.account_margin_level);
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Snapshot. Equity moves with price; don't cache it across time.
  • Currency. Every money field is in account_currency.
  • account_trade_mode is an i32 (0/1/2) — compare numerically.

docs.title: 🧪 Testing Suggestions
docs.text:
• Demo. account_trade_mode == 0; account_currency non-empty.
  • Flat account. account_equity == account_balance and account_margin == 0.

docs.title: 2. Orders & History — Overview
docs.text:
What's open now (market and pending orders, in one list), their ticket numbers, and the closed-order history.

In MT4 there are no separate "positions": a filled market order is the position, and pending orders sit in the same opened-orders list (distinguished by order_type). These methods are read-only and live on mt4_term_api.AccountHelper.

docs.title: Methods in this group
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner opened_orders(req) OpenedOrdersData All open market + pending orders, with full detail. opened_orders_tickets() OpenedOrdersTicketsData Just the ticket numbers (lightweight). orders_history(req) OrdersHistoryData Closed / cancelled orders over a time window (paged).

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text:
• "Show me everything open, with prices and P/L" → opened_orders() → order_infos.
  • "I just need the tickets to iterate" → opened_orders_tickets().
  • "What happened last week?" → orders_history() (time window + sort + paging).

Market orders vs pendings: filter order_infos by order_type — 0 Buy / 1 Sell are the market "positions"; 2..5 are the pending Limit/Stop types.

Back to: MT4Account — Master Overview

docs.title: Opened Orders (RECOMMENDED)
docs.text:
Everything currently live: open market orders and pending orders, with prices, SL/TP, profit and magic.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::opened_orders(request) (src/mt4/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: OpenedOrders(OpenedOrdersRequest) -> OpenedOrdersReply
  • Payload: OpenedOrdersData → order_infos: Vec<OpenedOrderInfo>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The full snapshot of your open book — market orders and pendings together.
  • Why you need it. Live P/L, SL/TP and volume per order — everything to manage trades.
  • When to use. Any position/order dashboard or management loop. This is what MT4Sugar's position helpers wrap.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn opened_orders(&self, request: pb::OpenedOrdersRequest) -> Result<pb::OpenedOrdersData, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message OpenedOrdersRequest { EnumOpenedOrderSortType sort_type = 1; }
message OpenedOrdersData { repeated OpenedOrderInfo order_infos = 1; }

docs.title: EnumOpenedOrderSortType
docs.text: Variant Value SortByOpenTimeAsc 0 SortByOpenTimeDesc 1 SortByOrderTicketIdAsc 2 SortByOrderTicketIdDesc 3

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OpenedOrderInfo (per order)
docs.text: Field Rust type Description ticket i32 Order ticket symbol String Symbol order_type i32 0 Buy, 1 Sell, 2 BuyLimit, 3 SellLimit, 4 BuyStop, 5 SellStop lots f64 Volume open_price f64 Open / trigger price stop_loss / take_profit f64 SL / TP (0 if unset) profit f64 Floating P/L swap f64 Accrued swap commision f64 Commission (proto spelling) magic_number i32 EA magic comment String Comment open_time / open_time_utc Option<Timestamp> Open time (server / UTC) expiration_time Option<Timestamp> Pending-order expiry

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One list, two kinds. Market orders (order_type 0/1) are the "positions"; 2–5 are pendings.
  • Sum profit + swap + commision for the true net floating result.
  • Snapshot. For live updates, stream on_opened_orders_profit.

docs.title: 1) Print open orders with P/L
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let d = account.opened_orders(pb::OpenedOrdersRequest { sort_type: pb::EnumOpenedOrderSortType::SortByOpenTimeAsc as i32 }).await?;
for o in &d.order_infos {
    let side = match o.order_type { 0 => "BUY", 1 => "SELL", _ => "PENDING" };
    println!("#{} {side} {} {:.2} lot  P/L {:+.2}", o.ticket, o.symbol, o.lots, o.profit);
}

docs.title: 2) Market positions only
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;
let d = account.opened_orders(pb::OpenedOrdersRequest { sort_type: 0 }).await?;
let positions: Vec<_> = d.order_infos.iter().filter(|o| o.order_type <= 1).collect();
println!("{} open positions", positions.len());

docs.title: 3) Total floating P/L
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;
let d = account.opened_orders(pb::OpenedOrdersRequest { sort_type: 0 }).await?;
let total: f64 = d.order_infos.iter().map(|o| o.profit + o.swap + o.commision).sum();
println!("floating P/L {total:+.2}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• sort_type is required — pass the enum as i32.
  • Pendings mixed in — filter by order_type when you mean "positions".
  • Snapshot. Re-query for fresh P/L.

Field Rust type Description ticket i32 Order ticket symbol String Symbol order_type i32 0 Buy … 5 SellStop lots f64 Volume open_price / close_price f64 Open / close price open_time / close_time (+ _utc) Option<Timestamp> Times stop_loss / take_profit f64 SL / TP profit / swap / commision f64 Result + costs magic_number i32 EA magic comment String Comment

docs.title: 1) Last 7 days, newest first
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;
fn ts(s: i64) -> prost_types::Timestamp { prost_types::Timestamp { seconds: s, nanos: 0 } }

let now = std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)?.as_secs() as i64;
let d = account.orders_history(pb::OrdersHistoryRequest {
    input_sort_mode: pb::EnumOrderHistorySortType::HistorySortByCloseTimeDesc as i32,
    input_from: Some(ts(now - 7 * 86_400)),
    input_to: Some(ts(now)),
    ..Default::default()
}).await?;
println!("{} rows (total {})", d.orders_info.len(), d.total_count);

docs.title: 2) Realized P/L over the window
docs.text:
let net: f64 = d.orders_info.iter().map(|o| o.profit + o.swap + o.commision).sum();
println!("net realized {net:+.2}");

docs.title: 3) Win rate
docs.text:
let wins = d.orders_info.iter().filter(|o| o.profit > 0.0).count();
if !d.orders_info.is_empty() { println!("win rate {:.1}%", wins as f64 / d.orders_info.len() as f64 * 100.0); }

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Server time. input_from/input_to are broker server time — mind the UTC offset (or use the _utc fields).
  • Paging. Large windows return total_count > rows; page with page_number/items_per_page (or page_token).
  • Costs. profit excludes swap/commission — sum them for net.

docs.title: 3. Symbols & Quotes — Overview
docs.text:
Everything about instruments and prices: the symbol list, Market Watch select, bulk contract params, live ticks, bar history, and the server timezone.

Mostly read-only (except symbol_select). Live on mt4_term_api.MarketInfo, AccountHelper (params / tick value) and ServerTimezone.

docs.title: Methods in this group
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner symbols() SymbolsData Every symbol name the terminal knows. symbol_select(req) SymbolSelectData Add / remove a symbol in Market Watch. symbol_params_many(req) SymbolParamsManyData Full contract params for one symbol or all. tick_value_with_size(req) TickValueWithSizeData Tick value / size / contract size per symbol. quote(req) QuoteData The latest tick (bid/ask + session high/low). quote_many(req) QuoteManyData Latest ticks for several symbols. quote_history(req) QuoteHistoryData OHLC bars for a symbol/timeframe range. server_timezone() ServerTimezoneData The broker server's UTC offset.

docs.title: When to use which
docs.text:
• "Is this symbol tradable?" → symbols() / symbol_select() → quote().
  • Contract specs (digits, point, volume rules, tick value) → symbol_params_many().
  • Money per tick → tick_value_with_size().
  • Candles / backtest input → quote_history() (MT4 timeframe enum: M1 = 0 … MN1 = 8).

MT4 has no per-property getters like MT5's symbol_info_double/integer/string — symbol_params_many returns the whole SymbolParamsManyInfo record at once.

pub async fn quote(&self, request: pb::QuoteRequest) -> Result<pb::QuoteData, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message QuoteRequest { string symbol = 1; }
message QuoteData {
  string symbol = 1;
  double bid = 2;
  double ask = 3;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp date_time = 4;      // broker server time
  google.protobuf.Timestamp date_time_utc = 7;
  double high = 5;                              // session high
  double low  = 6;                              // session low
}

docs.title: ⬇️ Input — QuoteRequest
docs.text: Field Rust type Description symbol String Exact symbol name; must be in Market Watch (symbol_select first)

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — QuoteData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description symbol String Echoed symbol bid / ask f64 Current bid / ask high / low f64 Session high / low date_time Option<Timestamp> Quote time (server) date_time_utc Option<Timestamp> Quote time (UTC)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Spread = ask − bid; divide by pip_size for spread in pips (MT4Sugar::spread_pips).
  • Mid price = (bid + ask) / 2 (MT4Sugar::mid_price).
  • Not selected → error. If the symbol isn't in Market Watch, select it (or use ensure_symbol) first.

docs.title: 1) Bid / ask / spread
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let q = account.quote(pb::QuoteRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
println!("bid {} ask {} spread {:.5}", q.bid, q.ask, q.ask - q.bid);

docs.title: 2) Guard: skip trading on a wide spread
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let q = account.quote(pb::QuoteRequest { symbol: "EURUSD".into() }).await?;
let spread_pips = (q.ask - q.bid) / (10.0 * 0.00001);
if spread_pips > 2.0 { println!("spread {spread_pips:.1} pips — skipping"); }

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Snapshot, not a stream. Re-call for a fresh price, or subscribe with on_symbol_tick.
  • Market closed. Over the weekend date_time may be stale — check it before acting.

docs.text:
OHLC bars for a symbol / timeframe over a time range — the input for backtests and indicators.

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. Historical candles (bars), not ticks.
  • Why you need it. Compute indicators, backtest, draw charts, seed a strategy's warm-up window.
  • When to use. On demand; range-limited by what the broker keeps on the server.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn quote_history(&self, request: pb::QuoteHistoryRequest) -> Result<pb::QuoteHistoryData, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message QuoteHistoryRequest {
  string symbol = 1;
  EnumQuoteHistoryTimeframe timeframe = 2;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp from_time = 3;      // server time  — send from_time OR from_time_utc
  google.protobuf.Timestamp from_time_utc = 5;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp to_time = 4;        // server time  — send to_time   OR to_time_utc
  google.protobuf.Timestamp to_time_utc = 6;
}
message QuoteHistoryData { repeated HistoryQuote historical_quotes = 1; }

docs.title: ⬇️ Input — QuoteHistoryRequest
docs.text: Field Rust type Description symbol String Exact symbol name timeframe i32 EnumQuoteHistoryTimeframe as i32 (see below) from_time / from_time_utc Option<Timestamp> Range start — send one of the two to_time / to_time_utc Option<Timestamp> Range end — send one of the two

docs.title: EnumQuoteHistoryTimeframe
docs.text:
Variant Value Period QhPeriodM1 0 1 minute QhPeriodM5 1 5 minutes QhPeriodM15 2 15 minutes QhPeriodM30 3 30 minutes QhPeriodH1 4 1 hour QhPeriodH4 5 4 hours QhPeriodD1 6 1 day QhPeriodW1 7 1 week QhPeriodMn1 8 1 month

⚠️ This is an ordinal enum (0–8), not MQL minute counts. H1 is 4, not 60.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — HistoryQuote (per bar)
docs.text: Field Rust type Description symbol String Symbol index i32 Bar index in the returned series time / time_utc Option<Timestamp> Bar open time (server / UTC) open / high / low / close f64 OHLC tick_volume i64 Tick count in the bar real_volume i64 Real volume (0 on most FX feeds) spread i32 Recorded spread, in points

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Pick UTC or server, not both for each bound — sending both is rejected.
  • Broker retention limits the range. Very old bars may simply not come back.
  • MT4Sugar::bars returns friendly Bar structs built on this call.

docs.title: 1) Last 100 H1 bars
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;
use prost_types::Timestamp;

let now = std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)?.as_secs() as i64;
let d = account.quote_history(pb::QuoteHistoryRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    timeframe: pb::EnumQuoteHistoryTimeframe::QhPeriodH1 as i32,
    from_time_utc: Some(Timestamp { seconds: now - 100 * 3600, nanos: 0 }),
    to_time_utc:   Some(Timestamp { seconds: now, nanos: 0 }),
    ..Default::default()
}).await?;
println!("{} bars", d.historical_quotes.len());

docs.title: 2) Highest high in the window
docs.text:
let hi = d.historical_quotes.iter().map(|b| b.high).fold(f64::MIN, f64::max);
println!("range high = {hi}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Enum, not minutes — timeframe: 60 is wrong (that's out of range); use QhPeriodH1 as i32 = 4.
  • Both bounds set in the same zone pair — use _utc fields together, or the server fields together.
  • Empty series = range outside broker retention or market never open there.

docs.title: Quote Many
docs.text:
Latest ticks for several symbols in one round-trip.

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. quote, batched — one call for a basket of symbols.
  • Why you need it. A watchlist, a correlation dashboard, or pricing a multi-symbol strategy without N round-trips.
  • When to use. Whenever you need more than one price at once.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn quote_many(&self, request: pb::QuoteManyRequest) -> Result<pb::QuoteManyData, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message QuoteManyRequest { repeated string symbols = 1; }
message QuoteManyData    { repeated QuoteData quotes = 1; }

docs.title: ⬇️ Input — QuoteManyRequest
docs.text: Field Rust type Description symbols Vec<String> Exact symbol names; each should be in Market Watch

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — QuoteManyData
docs.text:
Field Rust type Description quotes Vec<QuoteData> One QuoteData per symbol (same fields as quote)

Each QuoteData: symbol, bid, ask, high, low, date_time, date_time_utc.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Order isn't guaranteed. Match results by q.symbol, don't assume request order.
  • Missing symbols. A symbol not in Market Watch may be absent from the reply — select it first.

docs.title: 1) Price a watchlist
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let d = account.quote_many(pb::QuoteManyRequest {
    symbols: vec!["EURUSD".into(), "GBPUSD".into(), "USDJPY".into()],
}).await?;
for q in &d.quotes {
    println!("{:<8} {} / {}", q.symbol, q.bid, q.ask);
}

docs.title: 2) Build a symbol → mid-price map
docs.text:
use std::collections::HashMap;
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let d = account.quote_many(pb::QuoteManyRequest { symbols: vec!["EURUSD".into(), "GBPUSD".into()] }).await?;
let mids: HashMap<_, _> = d.quotes.iter().map(|q| (q.symbol.clone(), (q.bid + q.ask) / 2.0)).collect();
println!("{mids:?}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Match by name, not index.
  • Snapshot. For live multi-symbol prices, open one on_symbol_tick stream with all the names.

docs.title: Server Timezone
docs.text:
The broker server's UTC offset — so you can line up server-time fields with wall-clock UTC.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::server_timezone() (src/mt4/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.ServerTimezone
  • RPC: ServerTimezone(ServerTimezoneRequest) -> ServerTimezoneReply
  • Payload: ServerTimezoneData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. How many seconds east of UTC the broker server clock runs.
  • Why you need it. MT4 trade/quote timestamps are in server time; this offset converts them to UTC (most responses already carry a *_utc twin, but this lets you do it yourself).
  • When to use. Once after connecting; cache it.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn server_timezone(&self) -> Result<pb::ServerTimezoneData, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message ServerTimezoneRequest {}   // no arguments
message ServerTimezoneData {
  string server = 1;
  optional int32 utc_offset_seconds = 2;        // server time = UTC + this; multiple of 15 min
  ServerTimezoneSource source = 3;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp validated_utc = 4;
}

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — ServerTimezoneData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description server String Broker server name utc_offset_seconds Option<i32> Seconds east of UTC (server = UTC + offset). None when unknown; a present 0 means a genuine UTC+0 broker source i32 ServerTimezoneSource — where the offset came from validated_utc Option<Timestamp> When the offset was last validated from a fresh quote

docs.title: ServerTimezoneSource
docs.text: Variant Value Meaning Unknown 0 No terminal has read the offset yet (e.g. MT4 with the market closed); utc_offset_seconds / validated_utc stay unset Live 1 Read by this terminal itself LastValidated 2 Last offset validated for this broker, used until this terminal reads its own

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• None offset is real. When source = Unknown the broker's clock hasn't been read — prefer the *_utc fields on other responses, which stay correct.
  • Multiple of 15 minutes. Brokers sit on quarter-hour offsets (e.g. +10800 = UTC+3).
  • MT4Account caches server_utc_shift internally from this; you rarely convert by hand.

docs.title: 1) Print the offset
docs.text:
let tz = account.server_timezone().await?;
match tz.utc_offset_seconds {
    Some(s) => println!("{} is UTC{:+}", tz.server, s / 3600),
    None    => println!("{}: offset unknown (source {:?})", tz.server, tz.source),
}

docs.title: 2) Convert a server-time unix second to UTC
docs.text:
let tz = account.server_timezone().await?;
let offset = tz.utc_offset_seconds.unwrap_or(0) as i64;
let server_secs = 1_700_000_000_i64;        // some server-time stamp
let utc_secs = server_secs - offset;
println!("utc unix = {utc_secs}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Don't assume 0. Many brokers run UTC+2/+3 (with DST) — always read it.
  • Unknown ≠ zero. Treat None as "use the _utc fields", not "UTC+0".

docs.title: Symbol Params Many (RECOMMENDED)
docs.text:
The full contract specification for one symbol, or all of Market Watch — digits, point, volume rules, tick value, margin, swap, session data.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::symbol_params_many(request) (src/mt4/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: SymbolParamsMany(SymbolParamsManyRequest) -> SymbolParamsManyReply
  • Payload: SymbolParamsManyData → symbol_infos: Vec<SymbolParamsManyInfo>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MT4's one-shot replacement for MT5's per-property getters — the whole SymbolParamsManyInfo record at once.
  • Why you need it. digits / point for price math, volume_min/max/step for lot normalization, trade_tick_value for risk sizing, trade_stops_level for valid SL/TP distances.
  • When to use. Once per symbol at startup; cache the result.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_params_many(&self, request: pb::SymbolParamsManyRequest) -> Result<pb::SymbolParamsManyData, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolParamsManyRequest {
  optional string symbol_name = 1;   // one symbol; omit/None = all Market Watch symbols
}
message SymbolParamsManyData { repeated SymbolParamsManyInfo symbol_infos = 1; }

docs.title: ⬇️ Input — SymbolParamsManyRequest
docs.text: Field Rust type Description symbol_name Option<String> Some("EURUSD") for one symbol; None returns every symbol in Market Watch

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolParamsManyInfo (the fields you'll actually use)
docs.text:
Field Rust type Description symbol_name String Symbol this record describes digits i32 Price decimal places (5 for EURUSD, 3 for USDJPY) point f64 Smallest price step (0.00001 on a 5-digit symbol) volume_min / volume_max / volume_step f64 Lot bounds and increment volume_limit f64 Max total volume per symbol (0 = no limit) trade_tick_value f64 Money per tick for 1.0 lot (account currency) trade_tick_size f64 Price change that equals one tick trade_contract_size f64 Units per lot (100000 for FX majors) trade_stops_level i32 Min SL/TP distance from price, in points trade_freeze_level i32 Freeze distance where modify/close is blocked trade_mode i32 SpEnumSymbolTradeMode — disabled / long-only / short-only / close-only / full trade_calc_mode i32 SpEnumTradeCalcMode — 0 Forex, 1 CFD, 2 Futures, 3 CFD-index swap_long / swap_short f64 Swap charged per lot held overnight bid / ask f64 Last known bid/ask at the time of the call currency_base / currency_profit / currency_margin String The three symbol currencies sym_description / path String Human label and Market-Watch tree path

The record has ~60 fields (session stats, margin rates, ISIN, timestamps). The table lists the ones used in day-to-day automation.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Pips vs points. A pip is point × 10 on 3/5-digit symbols. MT4Sugar::pip_size does this for you.
  • Lot normalization. Round to volume_step and clamp to [volume_min, volume_max] — see MT4Sugar::normalize_lot.
  • Not selected? If a named symbol isn't in Market Watch the call adds it, then returns its record.

docs.title: 1) One symbol's trading rules
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let d = account.symbol_params_many(pb::SymbolParamsManyRequest {
    symbol_name: Some("EURUSD".into()),
}).await?;
let s = &d.symbol_infos[0];
println!("digits={} point={} step={} tick_value={}",
    s.digits, s.point, s.volume_step, s.trade_tick_value);

docs.title: 2) Normalize a lot to the symbol's step
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let s = account.symbol_params_many(pb::SymbolParamsManyRequest { symbol_name: Some("EURUSD".into()) })
    .await?.symbol_infos.into_iter().next().unwrap();
let want = 0.137_f64;
let lots = (want / s.volume_step).round() * s.volume_step;
let lots = lots.clamp(s.volume_min, s.volume_max);
println!("normalized lots = {lots}");

docs.title: 3) Dump every Market Watch symbol's digits
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;
let d = account.symbol_params_many(pb::SymbolParamsManyRequest { symbol_name: None }).await?;
for s in &d.symbol_infos { println!("{:<12} digits={}", s.symbol_name, s.digits); }

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Empty result for a bad name. A misspelled symbol yields no symbol_infos — check .first() before indexing.
  • trade_stops_level is in points. Multiply by point to get a price distance for SL/TP validation.
  • Cache it. These values rarely change intraday; don't call per tick.

docs.title: Symbol Select
docs.text:
Add a symbol to Market Watch (or remove it) so the terminal starts streaming its quotes.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::symbol_select(request) (src/mt4/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.MarketInfo
  • RPC: SymbolSelect(SymbolSelectRequest) -> SymbolSelectReply
  • Payload: SymbolSelectData → success: bool

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. The MQL SymbolSelect() — toggles a symbol in Market Watch.
  • Why you need it. A symbol not in Market Watch has no live quote; quote / order_send will fail until it's selected.
  • When to use. Before trading or quoting a symbol you haven't touched this session.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn symbol_select(&self, request: pb::SymbolSelectRequest) -> Result<pb::SymbolSelectData, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message SymbolSelectRequest {
  string symbol = 1;   // exact symbol name

}

docs.title: ⬇️ Input — SymbolSelectRequest
docs.text: Field Rust type Required Description symbol String ✅ Exact symbol name (from symbols()) select bool ✅ true to add, false to remove

docs.title: 1) Make a symbol tradable
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let d = account.symbol_select(pb::SymbolSelectRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    select: true,
}).await?;
assert!(d.success, "could not select EURUSD");

use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;
let _ = account.symbol_select(pb::SymbolSelectRequest { symbol: "GBPJPY".into(), select: false }).await?;

docs.text:
• Quote isn't instant. After select = true the first tick may take a moment — retry quote or use ensure_symbol.
  • Exact name only. "eurusd" or a wrong suffix returns success = false.

let d = account.symbols().await?;
println!("{} symbols", d.symbol_name_infos.len());

let d = account.symbols().await?;

    .map(|s| s.symbol_name.clone());

docs.title: Tick Value With Size
docs.text:
Money-per-tick, tick size and contract size for one or many symbols — the numbers behind risk sizing.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::tick_value_with_size(request) (src/mt4/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.AccountHelper
  • RPC: TickValueWithSize(TickValueWithSizeRequest) -> TickValueWithSizeReply
  • Payload: TickValueWithSizeData → infos: Vec<SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A focused slice of the contract spec: trade_tick_value, trade_tick_size, trade_contract_size.
  • Why you need it. Convert a stop distance in pips into cash risk, and cash risk into a lot size.
  • When to use. When sizing positions; lighter than pulling the full symbol_params_many record.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn tick_value_with_size(&self, request: pb::TickValueWithSizeRequest) -> Result<pb::TickValueWithSizeData, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message TickValueWithSizeRequest {
  repeated string symbol_names = 1;   // exact names; EMPTY = all Market Watch symbols
}
message TickValueWithSizeData { repeated SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo infos = 1; }

docs.title: ⬇️ Input — TickValueWithSizeRequest
docs.text: Field Rust type Description symbol_names Vec<String> Up to 1000 exact names. Empty = every symbol in Market Watch (not the whole server). Named symbols are added to Market Watch if missing.

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — SymbolTickValueWithSizeInfo (per symbol)
docs.text: Field Rust type Description index i32 Position in the request order symbol_name String Symbol trade_tick_value f64 Money per tick for 1.0 lot (account currency) trade_tick_size f64 Price move equal to one tick trade_contract_size f64 Units per lot

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Value per pip = trade_tick_value × (pip_size / trade_tick_size). On a 5-digit FX pair pip_size = 10 × point.
  • Lot from risk: lots = cash_risk / (stop_pips × pip_value_per_lot). MT4Sugar::calc_lot_by_risk wraps exactly this.
  • Name the symbols. Passing an empty list to "get everything" also forces every Market Watch symbol to refresh — prefer an explicit list.

docs.title: 1) Tick value for a basket
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let d = account.tick_value_with_size(pb::TickValueWithSizeRequest {
    symbol_names: vec!["EURUSD".into(), "GBPUSD".into()],
}).await?;
for i in &d.infos {
    println!("{:<8} tick_value={} tick_size={} contract={}",
        i.symbol_name, i.trade_tick_value, i.trade_tick_size, i.trade_contract_size);
}

docs.title: 2) Cash risk for a 20-pip stop on 0.10 lot
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let i = account.tick_value_with_size(pb::TickValueWithSizeRequest { symbol_names: vec!["EURUSD".into()] })
    .await?.infos.into_iter().next().unwrap();
let point = 0.00001;                      // from symbol_params_many
let pip = 10.0 * point;
let pip_value_per_lot = i.trade_tick_value * (pip / i.trade_tick_size);
let risk = 20.0 * pip_value_per_lot * 0.10;
println!("risk on 0.10 lot = {risk:.2}");

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Tick ≠ pip. trade_tick_value is per tick, not per pip — scale by pip_size / trade_tick_size.
  • Account currency. The value is already in your deposit currency; don't convert again.
  • ≤ 1000 names per call — a longer list is rejected with an error.

docs.text:
The write path: send, modify, and close/delete orders — plus close-by.

These are the only methods in MT4Account that change account state. They live on mt4_term_api.TradingHelper. Each takes the raw protobuf request (MT4's trade requests have several fields); friendlier shapes live in MT4Service and the order-construction helpers in MT4Sugar.

docs.title: Methods in this group
docs.text: Method Returns One-liner order_send(req) OrderSendData Open a market or pending order. order_modify(req) OrderModifyData Change SL/TP (open) or price/SL/TP/expiry (pending). order_close_delete(req) OrderCloseDeleteData Close a market order (full/partial) or delete a pending. order_close_by(req) OrderCloseByData Close an order by an opposite one.

docs.title: Trade errors
docs.text: Unlike the read methods, trade calls are not retried on transient errors (a timed-out OrderSend may have filled). MQL failures (130 invalid stops, 132 market closed, 134 not enough money, 138 requote, …) come back inside the reply's Error and surface as MT4Error::Api { mql_code, … }. MT4Sugar maps a non-zero mql_code to MT4Error::TradeError(code, message).

docs.title: A safe trading flow
docs.text:
1. Quote the symbol (quote / ensure_symbol) so it's live in Market Watch.
  2. Send (order_send) — check the reply.
  3. Manage (order_modify) — move SL to breakeven, trail.
  4. Close (order_close_delete, or order_close_by to net two opposite orders).

This is what the MT4Sugar orchestrators automate.

docs.title: Order Close By
docs.text:
Net two opposite orders on the same symbol against each other — close one by the other.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::order_close_by(request) (src/mt4/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • RPC: OrderCloseBy(OrderCloseByRequest) -> OrderCloseByReply
  • Payload: OrderCloseByData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL OrderCloseBy() — closes a buy against a sell (same symbol), saving one spread.
  • Why you need it. Flatten a hedged pair in a single operation instead of closing both at market.
  • When to use. You hold opposite positions on one symbol and want to net them.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn order_close_by(&self, request: pb::OrderCloseByRequest) -> Result<pb::OrderCloseByData, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message OrderCloseByRequest {
  int32 ticket_to_close = 1;            // the order being closed
  int32 opposite_ticket_closing_by = 2; // the opposite order used to close it
}
message OrderCloseByData {
  double close_price = 1;
  double profit = 2;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp close_time = 3;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp close_time_utc = 4;
}

docs.title: ⬇️ Input — OrderCloseByRequest
docs.text: Field Rust type Description ticket_to_close i32 The order you want closed opposite_ticket_closing_by i32 An opposite-side order on the same symbol used to close it

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCloseByData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description close_price f64 Price at which the netting happened profit f64 Realized P/L from the operation close_time / close_time_utc Option<Timestamp> Close time (server / UTC)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Same symbol, opposite side — a buy closes a sell and vice versa; different symbols are rejected.
  • Unequal volumes. If the two orders differ in size, the larger one leaves a remainder open (MT4 opens a new ticket for it).
  • Saves a spread versus two independent market closes.
  • Not all brokers allow it — some disable close-by; you'll get an MT4Error::Api.

docs.title: 1) Net a hedge
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let d = account.order_close_by(pb::OrderCloseByRequest {
    ticket_to_close: 123_456,            // the buy
    opposite_ticket_closing_by: 123_460, // the sell
}).await?;
println!("closed by @ {} profit {:+.2}", d.close_price, d.profit);

docs.title: 2) Guard before calling (confirm they're opposite on one symbol)
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let orders = account.opened_orders(pb::OpenedOrdersRequest { sort_type: 0 }).await?.order_infos;
let buy  = orders.iter().find(|o| o.symbol == "EURUSD" && o.order_type == 0);
let sell = orders.iter().find(|o| o.symbol == "EURUSD" && o.order_type == 1);
if let (Some(b), Some(s)) = (buy, sell) {
    account.order_close_by(pb::OrderCloseByRequest {
        ticket_to_close: b.ticket,
        opposite_ticket_closing_by: s.ticket,
    }).await?;
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Must be opposite + same symbol — otherwise rejected.
  • Volume remainder opens a fresh ticket; re-read opened_orders afterwards.
  • Broker support varies — handle the "not allowed" error.

docs.title: Order Close / Delete
docs.text:
Close a market order (full or partial) or delete a pending — one call, mode reported back.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::order_close_delete(request) (src/mt4/account.rs)

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL OrderClose() for market orders and OrderDelete() for pendings, merged — the server picks based on the ticket.
  • Why you need it. Exit a position or cancel a pending.
  • When to use. Closing out; partial close for scaling out.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn order_close_delete(&self, request: pb::OrderCloseDeleteRequest) -> Result<pb::OrderCloseDeleteData, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message OrderCloseDeleteRequest {
  int32  order_ticket = 1;             // required
  optional double lots = 2;            // market only; omit/None = full close
  optional double closing_price = 3;   // market only; omit = current market price
  optional int32  slippage = 4;        // points
}
message OrderCloseDeleteData {
  OrderCloseDeleteMode mode = 1;             // which action the server performed
  optional string history_order_comment = 2; // broker close comment, if any
}

docs.title: ⬇️ Input — OrderCloseDeleteRequest
docs.text: Field Rust type Description order_ticket i32 Ticket to close or delete (required) lots Option<f64> Market only — partial volume; None = close the whole order. Ignored for pendings closing_price Option<f64> Market only — explicit close price; None = market slippage Option<i32> Max deviation in points

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderCloseDeleteData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description mode i32 OrderCloseDeleteMode — what was done history_order_comment Option<String> Broker's comment on the resulting history order

docs.title: OrderCloseDeleteMode
docs.text: Variant Value Meaning OcdMarketOrder 0 A market order was closed OcdPendingOrder 1 A pending order was deleted

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• One call, two behaviours. Pass a market ticket → it closes; pass a pending ticket → it deletes. mode tells you which happened.
  • Partial close = set lots below the order volume (market orders only); the remainder stays open under a new ticket per MT4 rules.
  • Not retried on transient errors — reconcile with opened_orders on failure.

docs.title: 1) Full close of a position
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let d = account.order_close_delete(pb::OrderCloseDeleteRequest {
    order_ticket: 123_456,
    ..Default::default()
}).await?;
println!("mode = {:?}", d.mode);   // OcdMarketOrder

docs.title: 2) Partial close (scale out half)
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

account.order_close_delete(pb::OrderCloseDeleteRequest {
    order_ticket: 123_456,
    lots: Some(0.05),
    slippage: Some(20),
    ..Default::default()
}).await?;

docs.title: 3) Delete a pending
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;
let d = account.order_close_delete(pb::OrderCloseDeleteRequest { order_ticket: 123_457, ..Default::default() }).await?;
assert_eq!(d.mode, pb::OrderCloseDeleteMode::OcdPendingOrder as i32);

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• lots on a pending is ignored — pendings are deleted whole.
  • Partial remainder gets a new ticket. Track the returned state, don't assume the old ticket still holds the rest.
  • Close by price mismatch (129/138). Let closing_price default to market unless you have a reason not to.

docs.title: Order Modify
docs.text:
Change an order's SL/TP (open orders) or price/SL/TP/expiry (pendings).

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::order_modify(request) (src/mt4/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • RPC: OrderModify(OrderModifyRequest) -> OrderModifyReply
