docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL OrderModify() — adjust protective levels or a pending's trigger.
  • Why you need it. Move SL to breakeven, trail a stop, retarget a pending.
  • When to use. Managing a live order.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn order_modify(&self, request: pb::OrderModifyRequest) -> Result<pb::OrderModifyData, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message OrderModifyRequest {
  int32  order_ticket = 1;                 // required
  optional double new_price = 2;           // pendings only; ignored for open market orders
  optional double new_stop_loss = 3;
  optional double new_take_profit = 4;
  optional google.protobuf.Timestamp new_expiration = 5;      // pending expiry (server time)
  optional google.protobuf.Timestamp new_expiration_utc = 6;  // ...or UTC; not both
}
message OrderModifyData { bool order_was_modified = 1; }

docs.title: ⬇️ Input — OrderModifyRequest
docs.text: Field Rust type Description order_ticket i32 Ticket to modify (required) new_price Option<f64> New trigger price — pendings only; None leaves it new_stop_loss Option<f64> New SL price; None leaves it new_take_profit Option<f64> New TP price; None leaves it new_expiration / new_expiration_utc Option<Timestamp> New pending expiry — send one; None leaves it

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderModifyData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description order_was_modified bool true if the server accepted the change

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• None = unchanged. Only the fields you set are touched — safe partial updates.
  • "No changes" (error 1). Re-sending identical levels is rejected by MT4 as a no-op.
  • Stops distance (130). New SL/TP must respect trade_stops_level from symbol_params_many.
  • MT4Sugar exposes modify_sl_tp_by_price and modify_sl_tp_by_pips.

docs.title: 1) Move SL to breakeven
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let d = account.order_modify(pb::OrderModifyRequest {
    order_ticket: 123_456,
    new_stop_loss: Some(1.08500),   // = entry price
    ..Default::default()
}).await?;
println!("modified: {}", d.order_was_modified);

docs.title: 2) Retarget a pending's trigger price
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

account.order_modify(pb::OrderModifyRequest {
    order_ticket: 123_457,
    new_price: Some(1.07250),
    ..Default::default()
}).await?;

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Prices, not pips. Convert pip offsets to absolute prices first.
  • new_price on an open order is ignored — only SL/TP apply there.
  • Idempotent re-sends fail. Guard against sending the same values twice.

docs.title: Order Send (RECOMMENDED)
docs.text:
Open a market or pending order — the one write call that creates positions and pendings.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::order_send(request) (src/mt4/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.TradingHelper
  • RPC: OrderSend(OrderSendRequest) -> OrderSendReply
  • Payload: OrderSendData

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. MQL OrderSend() — market buy/sell or any of the four pendings.
  • Why you need it. It's how you enter the market.
  • When to use. Entry. SL/TP/comment/magic go in the same request.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn order_send(&self, request: pb::OrderSendRequest) -> Result<pb::OrderSendData, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message OrderSendRequest {
  string symbol = 1;                      // required, non-empty
  OrderSendOperationType operation_type = 2;  // required
  double volume = 3;                      // required, lots
  optional double price = 4;              // required for pendings; ignored for market
  optional int32  slippage = 5;           // points, default 0
  optional double stoploss = 6;           // price, default 0 = none
  optional double takeprofit = 7;         // price, default 0 = none
  optional string comment = 8;
  optional int32  magic_number = 9;
  optional google.protobuf.Timestamp expiration = 10;      // pending expiry (server time)
  optional google.protobuf.Timestamp expiration_utc = 11;  // ...or UTC; not both
}
message OrderSendData {
  int32  ticket = 1;
  double volume = 2;
  double price = 3;                       // actual fill / placement price
  google.protobuf.Timestamp open_time = 4;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp open_time_utc = 5;
}

docs.title: ⬇️ Input — OrderSendRequest
docs.text: Field Rust type Required Description symbol String ✅ Exact name, in Market Watch operation_type i32 ✅ OrderSendOperationType as i32 (below) volume f64 ✅ Lots (normalize to volume_step) price Option<f64> pendings Trigger price; None for market (fills at current bid/ask) slippage Option<i32> — Max deviation in points stoploss / takeprofit Option<f64> — SL / TP as prices; 0/None = none comment Option<String> — Free text magic_number Option<i32> — EA id for later filtering expiration / expiration_utc Option<Timestamp> — Pending expiry — send one

docs.title: OrderSendOperationType
docs.text: Variant Value Meaning OcOpBuy 0 Market buy OcOpSell 1 Market sell OcOpBuylimit 2 Buy limit (below price) OcOpSelllimit 3 Sell limit (above price) OcOpBuystop 4 Buy stop (above price) OcOpSellstop 5 Sell stop (below price)

docs.title: ⬆️ Output — OrderSendData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description ticket i32 New order ticket volume f64 Filled / placed volume price f64 Actual fill or placement price open_time / open_time_utc Option<Timestamp> Open time (server / UTC)

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Not retried. A timed-out order_send may already have filled — the layer never retries it blindly. Reconcile via opened_orders on error.
  • MQL failures (130 invalid stops, 132 market closed, 134 not enough money, 138 requote) come back in the reply's Error → MT4Error::Api { mql_code, .. }.
  • Respect trade_stops_level. SL/TP closer than the broker's minimum distance is rejected with 130.
  • MT4Sugar has buy_market / sell_limit / … that build this request for you.

docs.title: 1) Market buy with SL/TP
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let r = account.order_send(pb::OrderSendRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    operation_type: pb::OrderSendOperationType::OcOpBuy as i32,
    volume: 0.10,
    stoploss: Some(1.0800),
    takeprofit: Some(1.0900),
    slippage: Some(20),
    magic_number: Some(1001),
    comment: Some("demo".into()),
    ..Default::default()
}).await?;
println!("opened #{} @ {}", r.ticket, r.price);

docs.title: 2) Buy limit (pending) below the market
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let r = account.order_send(pb::OrderSendRequest {
    symbol: "EURUSD".into(),
    operation_type: pb::OrderSendOperationType::OcOpBuylimit as i32,
    volume: 0.10,
    price: Some(1.0750),
    ..Default::default()
}).await?;
println!("pending #{}", r.ticket);

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Pending needs price. Without it a pending request is invalid.
  • Prices, not pips. SL/TP are absolute prices — convert pip distances with pip_size first.
  • Don't double-send on timeout. Check opened_orders before retrying.

Real-time server-push streams: ticks, trade events, open-order ticket lists, per-order profit, and connection state.

while let Ok(Some(reply)) = stream.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_symbol_tick_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response {
        // handle d
    }
}

docs.title: On Connect State
docs.text:
Terminal connection-state events — know when the bridge to the broker goes up or down.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::on_connect_state(request) (src/mt4/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.Connection (note: not SubscriptionService)
  • RPC: OnConnectState(OnConnectStateRequest) -> stream OnConnectStateReply
  • Returns: tonic::Streaming<OnConnectStateReply>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A stream of connection-lifecycle updates for one or more terminals.
  • Why you need it. Pause trading while disconnected; alert on WrongPassword / Expired; drive reconnect logic.
  • When to use. Any long-running bot that must survive broker-side drops.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn on_connect_state(&self, request: pb::OnConnectStateRequest) -> Result<Streaming<pb::OnConnectStateReply>, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message OnConnectStateRequest { repeated string terminal_ids = 1; }  // empty = this terminal
message OnConnectStateReply { oneof response { ConnectStateData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }
message ConnectStateData {
  string id = 1;
  string state = 2;        // "Queued","Starting","Authorizing","Syncing","Connected","WrongPassword","Unreachable","Stopped","Expired"
  bool   is_connected = 3;
  bool   is_alive = 4;
  bool   api_is_alive = 5;
  string server = 6;
  uint64 account = 7;
  string error_message = 8;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp timestamp = 9;
}

docs.title: ⬇️ Input — OnConnectStateRequest
docs.text: Field Rust type Description terminal_ids Vec<String> Terminal GUIDs to watch; empty = this account's terminal

docs.title: ⬆️ Frame — ConnectStateData
docs.text:
Field Rust type Description id String Terminal id this update is about state String Human-readable state (see list above) is_connected bool Broker link is up is_alive bool Terminal process is alive api_is_alive bool API bridge is alive server String Broker server name account u64 Account login error_message String Populated on failure states timestamp Option<Timestamp> When the state was observed

state is a free-form string, not an enum — compare against the documented values.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Different service. This RPC lives on Connection, not SubscriptionService — the layer routes it correctly.
  • Gate trading on is_connected. Hold entries while it's false; resume on Connected.
  • Terminal states worth alerting on: WrongPassword, Expired, Unreachable, Stopped.
  • MT4Sugar exposes this via MT4Service::stream_connect_state.

docs.title: 1) Trade gate
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_connect_state(pb::OnConnectStateRequest { terminal_ids: vec![] }).await?;
while let Ok(Some(reply)) = s.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_connect_state_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response {
        println!("{} on {}: {} (connected={})", d.account, d.server, d.state, d.is_connected);
        if !d.is_connected { /* pause trading */ }
    }
}

docs.title: 2) Alert on auth failure
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_connect_state(pb::OnConnectStateRequest { terminal_ids: vec![] }).await?;
while let Ok(Some(reply)) = s.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_connect_state_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response {
        if d.state == "WrongPassword" || d.state == "Expired" {
            eprintln!("ALERT: {} — {}", d.state, d.error_message);
            break;
        }
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• state is a string — don't match it as an enum; watch for typos in comparisons.
  • Empty terminal_ids means "this terminal" — pass ids only when watching others.
  • Handle the Error arm and reconnect per your policy.

    timer_period_milliseconds: 1000,
}).await?;

docs.title: 2) Close-all on a drawdown limit
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_opened_orders_profit(pb::OnOpenedOrdersProfitRequest { timer_period_milliseconds: 1000 }).await?;
while let Ok(Some(reply)) = s.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_opened_orders_profit_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response {
        if let Some(a) = d.account_info {
            if a.profit < -100.0 {
                println!("drawdown hit {:+.2} — flatten now", a.profit);
                break;   // then close positions via order_close_delete
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls

docs.title: On Opened Orders Tickets
docs.text:
The list of open position and pending tickets, pushed on a timer.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::on_opened_orders_tickets(request) (src/mt4/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnOpenedOrdersTickets(OnOpenedOrdersTicketsRequest) -> stream OnOpenedOrdersTicketsReply
  • Returns: tonic::Streaming<OnOpenedOrdersTicketsReply>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A lightweight heartbeat of which tickets are open — positions and pendings, split into two lists.
  • Why you need it. Cheaply detect that the open set changed, then fetch detail only when it does.
  • When to use. A watchdog loop; a "did anything open/close?" trigger.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn on_opened_orders_tickets(&self, request: pb::OnOpenedOrdersTicketsRequest) -> Result<Streaming<pb::OnOpenedOrdersTicketsReply>, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message OnOpenedOrdersTicketsRequest { int32 pull_interval_milliseconds = 1; }
message OnOpenedOrdersTicketsReply { oneof response { OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }
message OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData {
  repeated int32 position_tickets = 1;
  repeated int32 pending_order_tickets = 2;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp server_time = 3;
  google.protobuf.Timestamp server_time_utc = 6;
  string terminal_instance_guid_id = 5;
}

docs.title: ⬇️ Input — OnOpenedOrdersTicketsRequest
docs.text: Field Rust type Description pull_interval_milliseconds i32 How often (ms) the server re-samples and pushes the list

docs.title: ⬆️ Frame — OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description position_tickets Vec<i32> Tickets of open market orders (positions) pending_order_tickets Vec<i32> Tickets of pending orders server_time / server_time_utc Option<Timestamp> Sample time (server / UTC) terminal_instance_guid_id String Emitting terminal

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Positions vs pendings are pre-split here (unlike opened_orders, where you filter by order_type).
  • Diff against the previous frame to spot opens/closes, then call opened_orders for the details of changed tickets.
  • pull_interval_milliseconds trades freshness for load — 500–2000 ms is typical.
  • MT4Sugar::watch_tickets wraps this into an mpsc channel.

docs.title: 1) React when the open set changes
docs.text:
use std::collections::BTreeSet;
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_opened_orders_tickets(pb::OnOpenedOrdersTicketsRequest {
    pull_interval_milliseconds: 1000,
}).await?;

let mut prev: BTreeSet<i32> = BTreeSet::new();
while let Ok(Some(reply)) = s.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_opened_orders_tickets_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response {
        let now: BTreeSet<i32> = d.position_tickets.iter().copied().collect();
        if now != prev {
            println!("positions changed: {:?}", now);
            prev = now;
        }
    }
}

docs.title: 2) Count open positions and pendings
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;
let mut s = account.on_opened_orders_tickets(pb::OnOpenedOrdersTicketsRequest { pull_interval_milliseconds: 2000 }).await?;
if let Ok(Some(reply)) = s.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_opened_orders_tickets_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response {
        println!("{} positions, {} pendings", d.position_tickets.len(), d.pending_order_tickets.len());
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Tickets only. No prices/P/L here — use on_opened_orders_profit or opened_orders for detail.
  • Interval too small = needless load; pick a sane cadence.
  • Handle the Error arm.

docs.title: On Symbol Tick (RECOMMENDED)
docs.text:
Live server-push ticks for one or more symbols — the real-time price feed.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::on_symbol_tick(request) (src/mt4/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnSymbolTick(OnSymbolTickRequest) -> stream OnSymbolTickReply
  • Returns: tonic::Streaming<OnSymbolTickReply>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A server stream that pushes a frame on every tick of the subscribed symbols.
  • Why you need it. Live prices without polling quote — lower latency, less load.
  • When to use. Dashboards, trailing logic, anything price-reactive. Drop the stream to unsubscribe.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn on_symbol_tick(&self, request: pb::OnSymbolTickRequest) -> Result<Streaming<pb::OnSymbolTickReply>, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message OnSymbolTickRequest { repeated string symbol_names = 1; }
message OnSymbolTickReply { oneof response { OnSymbolTickData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }
message OnSymbolTickData {
  OnSymbolMqlTickInfo symbol_tick = 1;
  string terminal_instance_guid_id = 2;
}

docs.title: ⬇️ Input — OnSymbolTickRequest
docs.text: Field Rust type Description symbol_names Vec<String> Symbols to stream; each must be in Market Watch

docs.title: ⬆️ Frame — OnSymbolTickData → symbol_tick: OnSymbolMqlTickInfo
docs.text:
Field Rust type Description symbol String Symbol this tick is for bid / ask f64 Current bid / ask last f64 Last deal price (where provided) volume u64 Volume for the last price time / time_utc Option<Timestamp> Tick time (server / UTC) time_msc / time_msc_utc i64 Tick time in milliseconds (server / UTC)

OnSymbolTickData also carries terminal_instance_guid_id — the terminal that emitted the tick.

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• Reading frames: loop on stream.message().await, match the oneof.
  • Unsubscribe = drop the Streaming value.
  • MT4Sugar::subscribe_quotes wraps this into an mpsc::Receiver<Quote> of friendly values.
  • Multiple symbols, one stream — subscribe once with the whole list.

docs.title: 1) Print ticks
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_symbol_tick(pb::OnSymbolTickRequest {
    symbol_names: vec!["EURUSD".into(), "GBPUSD".into()],
}).await?;

while let Ok(Some(reply)) = s.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_symbol_tick_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response {
        if let Some(t) = d.symbol_tick {
            println!("{:<8} {} / {}", t.symbol, t.bid, t.ask);
        }
    }
}

docs.title: 2) Stop after N ticks
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_symbol_tick(pb::OnSymbolTickRequest { symbol_names: vec!["EURUSD".into()] }).await?;
let mut n = 0;
while let Ok(Some(reply)) = s.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_symbol_tick_reply::Response::Data(_)) = reply.response {
        n += 1;
        if n >= 10 { break; }   // drop(s) on scope exit = unsubscribe
    }
}

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Select first. A symbol not in Market Watch produces no ticks — symbol_select / ensure_symbol.
  • Handle the Error arm — the server can push an error frame.
  • Quiet markets. No ticks ≠ broken stream; it's just no price change.

docs.title: On Trade
docs.text:
Order/trade events — new, changed and closed orders pushed as they happen.

API Information:

  • Low-level API: MT4Account::on_trade(request) (src/mt4/account.rs)
  • gRPC service: mt4_term_api.SubscriptionService
  • RPC: OnTrade(OnTradeRequest) -> stream OnTradeReply
  • Returns: tonic::Streaming<OnTradeReply>

docs.title: 💬 Just the essentials
docs.text:
• What it is. A stream of trade-book change events for the account.
  • Why you need it. React to fills, modifications and closes without re-polling opened_orders.
  • When to use. Event-driven bots, trade copiers, audit logs.

docs.title: Method Signature
docs.text:
pub async fn on_trade(&self, request: pb::OnTradeRequest) -> Result<Streaming<pb::OnTradeReply>, MT4Error>

Request / Reply:

message OnTradeRequest {}   // no arguments — subscribes to this account's events
message OnTradeReply { oneof response { OnTradeData data = 1; Error error = 2; } }
message OnTradeData {
  Mt4SubEnumEventGroupType type = 1;
  OnTadeEventData event_data = 2;
  OnEventAccountInfo account_info = 3;
  string terminal_instance_guid_id = 4;
}

docs.title: ⬆️ Frame — OnTradeData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description type i32 Mt4SubEnumEventGroupType — OrderProfit (0) or OrderUpdate (1) event_data Option<OnTadeEventData> The changed orders (below) account_info Option<OnEventAccountInfo> Balance / equity / margin snapshot at the event terminal_instance_guid_id String Emitting terminal

docs.title: OnTadeEventData
docs.text: Field Rust type Description new_orders Vec<OnTradeOrderInfo> Orders that just appeared updated_orders Vec<OnTradeUpdatedOrderInfo> Each has previous + current snapshots removed_orders Vec<OnTradeOrderInfo> Orders that were closed/deleted new_history_orders Vec<OnTradeOrderInfo> Newly archived history orders

docs.title: OnTradeOrderInfo (key fields)
docs.text: ticket · symbol · type (SubOrderOperationType 0–5) · lots · open_price · close_price · stop_loss · take_profit · order_profit · swap · commission · magic_number · comment · open_time/close_time (+ _utc) · is_history · account_login.

docs.title: Mt4SubEnumEventGroupType
docs.text: Variant Value OrderProfit 0 OrderUpdate 1

docs.title: 🧩 Notes & Tips
docs.text:
• updated_orders carries both sides — diff previous vs current to see what changed (SL moved, partially closed, …).
  • removed_orders is your "position closed" signal.
  • No request fields — the subscription is for the whole account.

docs.title: 1) Log fills and closes
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_trade(pb::OnTradeRequest {}).await?;
while let Ok(Some(reply)) = s.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_trade_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response {
        if let Some(ev) = d.event_data {
            for o in &ev.new_orders     { println!("NEW   #{} {} {:.2}", o.ticket, o.symbol, o.lots); }
            for o in &ev.removed_orders { println!("CLOSE #{} P/L {:+.2}", o.ticket, o.order_profit); }
        }
    }
}

docs.title: 2) Detect SL moves
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let mut s = account.on_trade(pb::OnTradeRequest {}).await?;
while let Ok(Some(reply)) = s.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_trade_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response {
        if let Some(ev) = d.event_data {
            for u in &ev.updated_orders {
                if let (Some(p), Some(c)) = (&u.previous, &u.current) {
                    if p.stop_loss != c.stop_loss {
                        println!("#{} SL {} -> {}", c.ticket, p.stop_loss, c.stop_loss);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

docs.text:
• Handle the Error arm.
  • Field is type → access as o.r#type in Rust (raw identifier).
  • Snapshot semantics. A single event may touch several lists — scan all four.

docs.text:
pub async fn orders_history(&self, sort: pb::EnumOrderHistorySortType, from: Option<Timestamp>, to: Option<Timestamp>)
    -> Result<pb::OrdersHistoryData, MT4Error>

Closed / cancelled orders over a time window. The service fills the paging defaults; you pass sort + bounds.

Arg — sort: EnumOrderHistorySortType

Variant Value HistorySortByOpenTimeAsc 0 HistorySortByOpenTimeDesc 1 HistorySortByCloseTimeAsc 2 HistorySortByCloseTimeDesc 3 HistorySortByOrderTicketIdAsc 4 HistorySortByOrderTicketIdDesc 5

Args: from / to — Option<Timestamp> server-time bounds (None = open-ended).

Returns: OrdersHistoryData → orders_info: Vec<HistoryOrderInfo>, total_count, next_page_token. Each HistoryOrderInfo: ticket, symbol, order_type, lots, open_price, close_price, open_time, close_time, profit, swap, commision, magic_number.

use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;
use prost_types::Timestamp;

let now = std::time::SystemTime::now().duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)?.as_secs() as i64;
let h = svc.orders_history(
    pb::EnumOrderHistorySortType::HistorySortByCloseTimeDesc,
    Some(Timestamp { seconds: now - 7 * 86_400, nanos: 0 }),
    Some(Timestamp { seconds: now, nanos: 0 }),
).await?;
let realized: f64 = h.orders_info.iter().map(|o| o.profit + o.swap + o.commision).sum();
println!("{} closed, realized {:+.2}", h.total_count, realized);

Paging: if next_page_token is non-empty there are more rows — request the next page with it (raw layer).

docs.title: MT4Service — 5. Streaming Methods
docs.text:
The five server streams, renamed to stream_* and taking friendly args. Each returns the raw tonic::Streaming<…Reply>; read with stream.message().await and match the reply's oneof { Data, Error }. Drop the stream to unsubscribe.

while let Ok(Some(reply)) = stream.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_symbol_tick_reply::Response::Data(d)) = reply.response { /* … */ }
}

MT4Sugar wraps the tick / profit / tickets streams into mpsc channels of friendly values — see MT4Sugar 8. Watchers & Waiters.

docs.title: stream_ticks(symbols)
docs.text:
pub async fn stream_ticks(&self, symbols: &[&str]) -> Result<Streaming<pb::OnSymbolTickReply>, MT4Error>

Live tick stream for a slice of symbols. Frame: OnSymbolTickData.symbol_tick → OnSymbolMqlTickInfo (symbol, bid, ask, last, volume, time).

use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;
let mut s = svc.stream_ticks(&["EURUSD", "GBPUSD"]).await?;
while let Ok(Some(r)) = s.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_symbol_tick_reply::Response::Data(d)) = r.response {
        if let Some(t) = d.symbol_tick { println!("{} {}/{}", t.symbol, t.bid, t.ask); }
    }
}

docs.title: stream_trades()
docs.text:
pub async fn stream_trades(&self) -> Result<Streaming<pb::OnTradeReply>, MT4Error>

Live order/trade events (new / updated / removed orders) for the account. Frame: OnTradeData → event_data (new_orders, updated_orders, removed_orders, new_history_orders) + account_info.

use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;
let mut s = svc.stream_trades().await?;
while let Ok(Some(r)) = s.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_trade_reply::Response::Data(d)) = r.response {
        if let Some(ev) = d.event_data {
            for o in &ev.removed_orders { println!("CLOSE #{} P/L {:+.2}", o.ticket, o.order_profit); }
        }
    }
}

docs.text:
pub async fn stream_opened_tickets(&self, interval_ms: i32) -> Result<Streaming<pb::OnOpenedOrdersTicketsReply>, MT4Error>

Open-order ticket list, pushed every interval_ms. Frame: OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData → position_tickets: Vec<i32>, pending_order_tickets: Vec<i32> (pre-split).

use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;
let mut s = svc.stream_opened_tickets(1000).await?;
if let Ok(Some(r)) = s.message().await {
    if let Some(pb::on_opened_orders_tickets_reply::Response::Data(d)) = r.response {
        println!("{} positions, {} pendings", d.position_tickets.len(), d.pending_order_tickets.len());
    }
}

pub async fn stream_opened_profit(&self, interval_ms: i32) -> Result<Streaming<pb::OnOpenedOrdersProfitReply>, MT4Error>

Per-order floating profit + account snapshot, pushed every interval_ms. Frame: OnOpenedOrdersProfitData → opened_orders_with_profit_updated, account_info (equity, profit, margin_level).

use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

while let Ok(Some(r)) = s.message().await {

docs.title: MT4Service — Mid-Level API Overview
docs.text:
The friendly facade over MT4Account: the same operations, but you pass plain arguments (&str symbols, tickets, typed sort enums) and get back clean values instead of hand-built …Request structs.

Defined in src/mt4/service.rs. It wraps one MT4Account (field acc); borrow it with service.account() / service.account_mut().

MT4Sugar (HIGH)   order building, pip math, risk sizing, one-liners
   │ uses
MT4Service (MID)  ← you are here — friendly args, clean returns
   │ uses
MT4Account (LOW)  raw gRPC, …Data payloads

The value-add is two conveniences: friendly arguments (build the …Request and cast enums for you) and clean returns (simple getters unwrap …Data to a scalar/Vec). Streaming methods are renamed to stream_* and return the raw tonic::Streaming<…Reply>.

docs.title: Usage pattern
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::{MT4Account, MT4Service};
use metarpc_mt4::mt4_term_api as pb;

let svc = MT4Service::new(MT4Account::new("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443));

let balance = svc.account_summary().await?.account_balance;      // field off the typed data
let selected = svc.symbol_select("EURUSD", true).await?;         // bool
let q = svc.quote("EURUSD").await?;                              // QuoteData
let open = svc.opened_orders(pb::EnumOpenedOrderSortType::SortByOpenTimeAsc).await?; // Vec

docs.text:

docs.text:
pub fn set_defaults(self, magic: i32, slippage: u32, comment: impl Into<String>) -> Self

Builder — sets the defaults the Order Entry helpers stamp onto each order. Returns self, so chain it after new.

use metarpc_mt4::{MT4Account, MT4Service, MT4Sugar};

let sugar = MT4Sugar::new(MT4Service::new(MT4Account::new("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443)))
    .set_defaults(1001, 20, "my-bot");   // magic 1001, 20-point slippage, comment "my-bot"

magic = 0 means "don't stamp a magic"; an empty comment means "don't stamp a comment".

pub async fn ensure_symbol(&self, symbol: &str, wait: Duration) -> Result<Quote, MT4Error>

docs.text:
pub async fn bars(&self, symbol: &str, timeframe: i32, count: usize) -> Result<Vec<Bar>, MT4Error>

The newest count bars of timeframe, oldest first. timeframe is an EnumQuoteHistoryTimeframe value (M1 = 0 … MN1 = 8). Returns Vec<Bar> = { time, open, high, low, close, tick_volume, real_volume, spread }.

let hi = bars.iter().map(|b| b.high).fold(f64::MIN, f64::max);

docs.title: MT4Sugar — 4. Risk Sizing
docs.text: Turn a stop distance into cash risk, and a cash-risk budget into a normalized lot size. Both use the symbol's pip value per lot (trade_tick_value × pip_size / trade_tick_size).

docs.title: calc_cash_risk(symbol, lots, sl_pips)
docs.text:
pub async fn calc_cash_risk(&self, symbol: &str, lots: f64, sl_pips: f64) -> Result<f64, MT4Error>

How much deposit currency you'd lose if lots is stopped out sl_pips away.

cash = lots × sl_pips × pip_value_per_lot

let risk = sugar.calc_cash_risk("EURUSD", 0.10, 20.0).await?;
println!("risking {risk:.2} on 0.10 lot / 20 pips");

docs.title: calc_lot_by_risk(symbol, risk_cash, sl_pips)
docs.text:
pub async fn calc_lot_by_risk(&self, symbol: &str, risk_cash: f64, sl_pips: f64) -> Result<f64, MT4Error>

The inverse: the normalized lot size that risks risk_cash over an sl_pips stop.

lots = risk_cash / (sl_pips × pip_value_per_lot) → rounded to volume_step, clamped to [min, max].

Guards: if sl_pips <= 0 or pip value is unknown, it returns the symbol's minimum normalized lot rather than erroring.

// Risk 1% of balance on a 20-pip stop
let bal = sugar.get_account_info().await?.balance;
let lots = sugar.calc_lot_by_risk("EURUSD", bal * 0.01, 20.0).await?;
let r = sugar.buy_market("EURUSD", lots, None, None).await?;
println!("opened #{} with {lots} lot", r.ticket);

Typical flow: pick a stop in pips → calc_lot_by_risk for the volume → buy_market / sell_market → set SL/TP with modify_sl_tp_by_pips. The Strategies orchestrators chain exactly this.

docs.title: MT4Sugar — 5. Order Entry
docs.text:
Open positions and pendings by side + lots — no hand-built OrderSendRequest. Each helper stamps the default magic / slippage / comment (from set_defaults) and returns an OrderResult.

OrderResult = { ticket, error_code, price, lots, open_time, message }. On success error_code = 0; MQL failures come back as MT4Error::TradeError(code, msg).

sl / tp are absolute prices (Option<f64>). Convert pip distances with pips_to_price first, or open without stops and set them with modify_sl_tp_by_pips.

pub async fn place_order(&self, req: OrderRequest) -> Result<OrderResult, MT4Error>

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• "No changes" (error 1). Re-sending identical levels is rejected — track current SL/TP.
  • Order must be open. modify_sl_tp_by_pips errors if the ticket isn't currently open.
  • Bulk ops are best-effort. close_all / cancel_pendings count successes; a single failure doesn't abort the rest.

docs.title: MT4Sugar — 7. Trailing & Breakeven
docs.text: Two one-shot stop-management primitives. Each inspects the position once, moves the stop only in the safe direction, and returns whether it moved. Call them on a timer to keep them active — they hold no background state themselves.

docs.title: auto_breakeven(ticket, trigger_pips, plus_pips)
docs.text:
pub async fn auto_breakeven(&self, ticket: u64, trigger_pips: f64, plus_pips: f64) -> Result<bool, MT4Error>

Once the position is at least trigger_pips in profit, move its stop to entry ± plus_pips (a small lock-in above/below the open price). Never loosens an existing stop. Returns true if the stop was moved this call.

  • trigger_pips — how much profit before breakeven arms.
  • plus_pips — where the new stop sits relative to entry (0 = exact breakeven, positive = locked profit).
// Arm at +10 pips, lock +2 pips of profit
let moved = sugar.auto_breakeven(123_456, 10.0, 2.0).await?;
if moved { println!("stop moved to breakeven+2"); }

docs.title: trail_stop(ticket, distance_pips)
docs.text:
pub async fn trail_stop(&self, ticket: u64, distance_pips: f64) -> Result<bool, MT4Error>

Ratchet the stop to distance_pips behind the current price, only ever tightening. Returns true if the stop was moved this call.

let moved = sugar.trail_stop(123_456, 15.0).await?;   // trail 15 pips behind

docs.title: Running them continuously
docs.text:
Both are one-shot — drive them from a loop:

use std::time::Duration;

loop {
    if sugar.find_ticket(123_456).await?.is_none() { break; }   // closed → stop
    sugar.auto_breakeven(123_456, 10.0, 2.0).await?;
    sugar.trail_stop(123_456, 15.0).await?;
    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_secs(2)).await;
}

This is exactly what the Strategies manage() worker does — with an activation gate so trailing starts only after a configured profit.

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Direction-safe by design. Neither will ever widen risk; a call that would loosen the stop returns false and does nothing.
  • Needs a live quote. Both read last_quote; on a dead feed they'll error — pair with ensure_symbol.
  • Respect stops level. A trail closer than trade_stops_level is rejected by the broker (130).

See also: 6. Order Management · 8. Watchers & Waiters · MT4Sugar — Master Overview

docs.title: MT4Sugar — 8. Watchers & Waiters
docs.text:
Watchers wrap a gRPC stream into a tokio::mpsc channel of friendly values (a background task forwards frames). Waiters poll until a condition holds or a timeout elapses.

The background task of a watcher ends on the first stream error or when you drop the receiver.

docs.title: subscribe_quotes(symbols)
docs.text:
pub async fn subscribe_quotes(&self, symbols: Vec<String>) -> Result<mpsc::Receiver<Quote>, MT4Error>

Live ticks for symbols, delivered as Quotes.

let mut rx = sugar.subscribe_quotes(vec!["EURUSD".into(), "GBPUSD".into()]).await?;
while let Some(q) = rx.recv().await {
    println!("{:<8} {}/{}", q.symbol, q.bid, q.ask);
}

docs.title: watch_profit(interval_ms)
docs.text:
pub async fn watch_profit(&self, interval_ms: i32) -> Result<mpsc::Receiver<pb::OnOpenedOrdersProfitData>, MT4Error>

Per-order floating profit + account snapshot every interval_ms. Each item is the raw OnOpenedOrdersProfitData (account_info.equity, account_info.profit, opened_orders_with_profit_updated).

let mut rx = sugar.watch_profit(1000).await?;
while let Some(d) = rx.recv().await {
    if let Some(a) = d.account_info { println!("equity {:.2} floating {:+.2}", a.equity, a.profit); }
}

docs.title: watch_tickets(interval_ms)
docs.text:
pub async fn watch_tickets(&self, interval_ms: i32) -> Result<mpsc::Receiver<pb::OnOpenedOrdersTicketsData>, MT4Error>

The open-order ticket list every interval_ms (position_tickets, pending_order_tickets, pre-split).

let mut rx = sugar.watch_tickets(1000).await?;
while let Some(d) = rx.recv().await {
    println!("{} positions, {} pendings", d.position_tickets.len(), d.pending_order_tickets.len());
}

docs.title: wait_price(symbol, target, above, timeout)
docs.text:
pub async fn wait_price(&self, symbol: &str, target: f64, above: bool, timeout: Duration) -> Result<Quote, MT4Error>

Poll until the price reaches target — above = true waits for bid ≥ target, false for ask ≤ target. Returns the triggering [Quote], or errors on timeout.

use std::time::Duration;
let q = sugar.wait_price("EURUSD", 1.0900, true, Duration::from_secs(60)).await?;
println!("hit {} at bid {}", 1.0900, q.bid);

docs.title: wait_filled(ticket, timeout)
docs.text:
pub async fn wait_filled(&self, ticket: u64, timeout: Duration) -> Result<bool, MT4Error>

Poll until a pending ticket becomes a market order (filled). true on fill, false on timeout.

use std::time::Duration;
if sugar.wait_filled(123_457, Duration::from_secs(300)).await? {
    println!("pending filled");
}

docs.title: wait_closed(ticket, timeout)
docs.text:
pub async fn wait_closed(&self, ticket: u64, timeout: Duration) -> Result<bool, MT4Error>

Poll until ticket is no longer open (closed or deleted). true on close, false on timeout.

use std::time::Duration;
sugar.wait_closed(123_456, Duration::from_secs(120)).await?;

docs.title: ⚠️ Pitfalls
docs.text:
• Watchers vs waiters. Watchers push continuously (keep the receiver alive); waiters return once.
  • Waiters poll every 500 ms — they're convenience, not low-latency triggers. For hot paths use subscribe_quotes.
  • Drop to unsubscribe. Dropping the Receiver ends the watcher's background task.

docs.title: MT4Sugar — 9. Order Info
docs.text:
Read the open book and account state — filtered views, lookups, P/L sums, exposure, and a compact account snapshot.

In MT4 an open market order is a position; pendings sit in the same list, told apart by order_type (0 Buy, 1 Sell = market; 2–5 = pending).

docs.text:

All open market + pending orders (sorted by open time asc).

pub async fn positions(&self) -> Result<Vec<pb::OpenedOrderInfo>, MT4Error>

Open market orders only — MT4's equivalent of "positions".

println!("{} positions open", sugar.positions().await?.len());

One open order by ticket, or None if it isn't open.

docs.title: total_profit(symbol)
docs.text:
pub async fn total_profit(&self, symbol: Option<&str>) -> Result<f64, MT4Error>

Total floating profit across open positions (profit + swap + commision), optionally for one symbol.

println!("floating P/L: {:+.2}", sugar.total_profit(None).await?);

docs.text:
pub async fn positions_value(&self, symbol: Option<&str>, magic: Option<i32>) -> Result<f64, MT4Error>

Floating value of positions filtered by symbol and/or magic (None = don't filter on that axis). Includes swap and commission.

let v = sugar.positions_value(Some("EURUSD"), Some(1001)).await?;

docs.text:
pub async fn exposure_summary(&self) -> Result<Vec<(String, f64)>, MT4Error>

Net lots per symbol across open market positions — buy positive, sell negative. Sorted by symbol.

for (sym, net) in sugar.exposure_summary().await? {

docs.title: get_account_info()
docs.text:
pub async fn get_account_info(&self) -> Result<AccountInfo, MT4Error>

A compact AccountInfo snapshot: login, currency, balance, equity, credit, leverage, name, company, trade_mode, is_investor, server_time, utc_shift_minutes.

let a = sugar.get_account_info().await?;
println!("{} {} — balance {:.2}", a.login, a.currency, a.balance);

docs.title: MT4Sugar — Master Overview
docs.text:
High-level, one-line convenience methods for MetaTrader 4 automation in Rust.

MT4Sugar wraps an MT4Service (composition) and adds ergonomic business logic: quick prices, symbol math, risk-based lot sizing, order construction from side/lots, order management, trailing/breakeven, live watchers and account info. Defined in src/mt4/sugar.rs.

It reuses the plain DTOs in crate::models: Quote, Bar, OrderRequest, OrderResult, CloseResult, AccountInfo, OrderType.

MT4Sugar (HIGH)  ← you are here
   │ uses  MT4Service (MID) → MT4Account (LOW) → gRPC → MT4 terminal

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Pips. A pip is point × 10 on 3/5-digit symbols, else point.
  • Defaults. MT4Sugar::new(svc).set_defaults(magic, slippage, comment) sets the magic / slippage / comment used by the order-entry helpers.
  • Orders, not positions. MT4's open market orders are the "positions"; orders() returns everything, positions() the market ones.
  • Async. Every method is async — .await it.

docs.title: Strategies — Presets
docs.text: The two builder types that configure every orchestrator, plus the ready-made catalog. Defined in src/strategies/mod.rs.

docs.title: StrategyPreset
docs.text:
WHAT to trade. A fluent builder.

Field Type Meaning symbol String Instrument use_market bool true = market entry, false = pending limit entry_price Option<f64> Limit price (when not market) lots Option<f64> Fixed volume; None = size by risk % magic i32 EA magic stamped on the order comment String Order comment

Builder methods:

StrategyPreset::new("EURUSD")   // defaults: market, no fixed lots, magic 0
    .market()                   // market entry (clears entry_price)
    .limit_at(1.0750)           // ...or a BUY LIMIT at a price
    .lots(0.10)                 // fixed volume (skip risk sizing)
    .magic(777)
    .comment("my setup");

Leave .lots() unset to let the orchestrator size by the RiskPreset's risk %.

docs.title: RiskPreset
docs.text:
HOW MUCH to risk and how to protect. A fluent builder.

Field Type Meaning risk_percent f64 % of balance to risk when sizing by risk sl_pips f64 Stop-loss distance in pips (also the risk denominator) tp_pips Option<f64> Take-profit distance in pips trailing_pips Option<f64> Trailing distance; None = no trailing be_trigger_pips Option<f64> Profit at which breakeven arms be_plus_pips f64 Pips of profit locked at breakeven (0 = exact BE)

Builder methods:

RiskPreset::new(1.0, 20.0)      // 1% risk, 20-pip stop
    .tp(40.0)                   // 40-pip target
    .trailing(15.0)             // trail 15 pips behind
    .breakeven(10.0, 2.0);      // arm BE at +10p, lock +2p

docs.text: Ready-made builders you can pass straight to an orchestrator:

docs.title: Strategy presets
docs.text: Fn Builds market_eurusd() Market EURUSD, magic 777 limit_eurusd(price) BUY LIMIT EURUSD at price, magic 778

docs.title: Risk presets
How the presets drive sizing
docs.text:
The orchestrators call size_lot:

  • StrategyPreset.lots = Some(x) → use x directly.
  • lots = None → calc_lot_by_risk(symbol, balance × risk_percent / 100, sl_pips) — the normalized lot that risks risk_percent of balance over the stop.

docs.title: Strategies — Master Overview
docs.text:
Ready-made orchestrators that chain MT4Sugar calls into a full trade lifecycle — size → enter → manage → close — driven by two small preset types.

Defined in src/strategies/. Each orchestrator is a plain async fn run_*(sugar, …).

docs.title: ⚠️ Demonstration templates only
docs.text: These orchestrators are teaching examples — run them on DEMO accounts. They show how to compose the SDK into a lifecycle; they are not production trading systems. There is no market analysis, no portfolio risk control, no drawdown guard, and the management window is a short fixed timer. Use them as a skeleton and add your own edge, risk rules and supervision before anything live.

docs.title: The two presets
docs.text:
A strategy is what to trade + how much to risk:

  • StrategyPreset — WHAT: symbol, market vs limit entry, optional fixed lots, magic, comment.
  • RiskPreset — HOW MUCH: risk %, SL/TP in pips, optional trailing and breakeven.

Catalog of ready builders: market_eurusd(), limit_eurusd(price), conservative(), balanced(), aggressive() — see Presets.

docs.title: The three orchestrators
docs.text:
Orchestrator Entry Management Page Market One-Shot market BUY breakeven + trail (from preset), ~5 s market_one_shot Bracket + Trailing market BUY + bracket trail starts only after a profit cushion, ~10 s bracket_trailing Pending Bracket BUY LIMIT, wait for fill (or cancel) breakeven + trail after fill pending_bracket

All three: size the lot (fixed or by risk %), enter, apply a pip-based SL/TP bracket, run the shared manage() worker, then flatten.

docs.title: Shared building blocks
docs.text:
• size_lot(sugar, sp, rp) — fixed sp.lots if set, else calc_lot_by_risk(balance × risk% , sl_pips).
  • manage(sugar, ticket, symbol, rp, secs, trail_activate_pips) — for secs, repeatedly: apply auto_breakeven (from be_trigger_pips) and, once at least trail_activate_pips in profit, trail_stop. Returns early if the order closed (SL/TP hit). Polls every 500 ms.

docs.title: Minimal usage
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::{MT4Account, MT4Service, MT4Sugar};
use metarpc_mt4::strategies::{run_market_one_shot, market_eurusd, balanced};

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let sugar = MT4Sugar::new(MT4Service::new(MT4Account::new("mt4.mrpc.pro", 443)))
        .set_defaults(777, 20, "demo");
    sugar.connect_by_server_name(12_345_678, "password", "FreshForex-Demo", None, 120).await?;

    let sp = market_eurusd();   // WHAT: market EURUSD, magic 777
    let rp = balanced();        // HOW: 1% risk, SL 20 / TP 40, trail 15, BE 10/+2
    let ticket = run_market_one_shot(&sugar, &sp, &rp).await?;
    println!("done, ticket {ticket}");

    sugar.disconnect(false).await?;
    Ok(())
}

The runnable version is examples/4_strategies/strategies_demo.rs — gated behind STRATEGY_RUN=1.

docs.title: Orchestrator — Bracket + Trailing
docs.text:
Enter with a bracket, then start trailing only after the trade earns a cushion. src/strategies/bracket_trailing.rs.

pub async fn run_bracket_trailing(sugar: &MT4Sugar, sp: &StrategyPreset, rp: &RiskPreset, activate_at_pips: f64) -> Result<u64, MT4Error>

Extra arg: activate_at_pips — trailing stays off until the position is this many pips in profit.

Returns: the order ticket.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Size — size_lot(sugar, sp, rp).
  2. Enter — buy_market(symbol, lots, None, None).
  3. Bracket — modify_sl_tp_by_pips(ticket, Some(sl_pips), tp_pips).
  4. Manage — manage() for ~10 seconds, passing activate_at_pips as the trail activation gate. Auto-breakeven (from be_trigger_pips) still applies earlier; trailing waits for the cushion.
  5. Close — close(ticket, None).

docs.title: Why the activation gate
docs.text: Trailing immediately from entry often gets stopped out by normal spread/noise before the trade develops. Gating it behind activate_at_pips lets the position breathe, then protects profit once it's real — while breakeven still arms as soon as be_trigger_pips is hit.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::strategies::{run_bracket_trailing, market_eurusd, balanced};

let sp = market_eurusd();
let rp = balanced();                 // trail 15, BE 10/+2
let ticket = run_bracket_trailing(&sugar, &sp, &rp, 12.0).await?;  // trail arms at +12 pips

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Needs trailing_pips set in the RiskPreset for the gate to matter (balanced() / aggressive() set it; conservative() does not).
  • Longer window (~10 s) than Market One-Shot, to give the cushion time to form in the demo.

See also: Strategies — Master Overview · market_one_shot · pending_bracket

docs.title: Orchestrator — Market One-Shot
docs.text:
The simplest lifecycle: size → market BUY → pip bracket → manage briefly → close. src/strategies/market_one_shot.rs.

pub async fn run_market_one_shot(sugar: &MT4Sugar, sp: &StrategyPreset, rp: &RiskPreset) -> Result<u64, MT4Error>

Returns: the order ticket.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Size — size_lot(sugar, sp, rp) (fixed sp.lots, else risk-based).
  2. Enter — buy_market(symbol, lots, None, None).
  3. Bracket — modify_sl_tp_by_pips(ticket, Some(sl_pips), tp_pips) from the RiskPreset.
  4. Manage — the shared manage() worker for ~5 seconds; trailing activates from be_trigger_pips (or 0 if unset), breakeven from be_trigger_pips.
  5. Close — close(ticket, None) and return the ticket.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::strategies::{run_market_one_shot, market_eurusd, balanced};

let sp = market_eurusd();
let rp = balanced();
let ticket = run_market_one_shot(&sugar, &sp, &rp).await?;
println!("ran one-shot, ticket {ticket}");

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• BUY-side demo. Like all three templates it enters long; mirror the logic for shorts.
  • Fixed management window. The ~5 s timer is for demonstration — a real strategy manages until an exit signal, not a clock.
  • Early exit. If SL/TP fills during management, manage() returns as soon as the ticket is gone; the final close then no-ops.

See also: Strategies — Master Overview · bracket_trailing · pending_bracket

docs.title: Orchestrator — Pending Bracket
docs.text:
Place a BUY LIMIT, wait for the fill (or cancel on timeout), then bracket and manage. src/strategies/pending_bracket.rs.

pub async fn run_pending_bracket(sugar: &MT4Sugar, sp: &StrategyPreset, rp: &RiskPreset, timeout_seconds: u64) -> Result<u64, MT4Error>

Extra arg: timeout_seconds — how long to wait for the pending to fill before cancelling it.

Returns: the order ticket (filled-and-managed, or the cancelled pending).

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
1. Entry price — sp.entry_price if set, else 5 pips below current bid (demo default).
  2. Size — size_lot(sugar, sp, rp).
  3. Place — buy_limit(symbol, lots, entry, None, None).
  4. Wait — wait_filled(ticket, timeout_seconds):
  5. Not filled in time → close(ticket, None) deletes the resting pending, return the ticket.
  6. Filled → continue.
  7. Bracket — modify_sl_tp_by_pips(ticket, Some(sl_pips), tp_pips).
  8. Manage — manage() for ~5 seconds (trail from be_trigger_pips).
  9. Close — close(ticket, None).

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
use metarpc_mt4::strategies::{run_pending_bracket, limit_eurusd, conservative};

// Explicit limit price via the preset
let sp = limit_eurusd(1.0750);
let rp = conservative();
let ticket = run_pending_bracket(&sugar, &sp, &rp, 60).await?;   // wait up to 60s for the fill

Or let it pick the demo entry (5 pips below bid):

use metarpc_mt4::strategies::{run_pending_bracket, market_eurusd, balanced};
let sp = market_eurusd();   // no entry_price → 5 pips below bid
run_pending_bracket(&sugar, &sp, &balanced(), 30).await?;

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Fill detection = the ticket's order_type flipping from BuyLimit (2) to Buy (0); wait_filled polls every 500 ms.
  • Cancel is a close. Deleting a resting pending uses the same order_close_delete path (mode = pending deleted).
  • Timeout returns the ticket anyway — check whether it filled via your own state if you need to branch.
